passages.original: No, you’ll reveal it.
passages.vernacular: 唔,你會洩露。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,你會洩露。

passages.title: Horatio 霍拉旭
passages.original: Not I, my lord, by heaven.
passages.vernacular: 我唔會,殿下,憑天發誓。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不會,殿下,憑天發誓。

passages.title: Marcellus 馬賽勒斯
passages.original: Nor I, my lord.
passages.vernacular: 我亦唔會,殿下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我也不會,殿下。

passages.title: Hamlet 哈姆雷特
passages.original: How say you then, would heart of man once think it?— But you’ll be secret?
passages.vernacular: 咁你哋點講,人心會唔會一度想到?——不過你哋會保密嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那你們怎麼說,人心會不會一度想到?——不過你們會保密嗎?

passages.title: Horatio And Marcellus 霍拉旭同馬賽勒斯
passages.original: Ay, by heaven, my lord.
passages.vernacular: 會,憑天發誓,殿下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 會,憑天發誓,殿下。

passages.title: Hamlet 哈姆雷特
passages.original: There’s ne’er a villain dwelling in all Denmark But he’s an arrant knave.
passages.vernacular: 全丹麥冇一個住喺度嘅惡棍,唔係個徹頭徹尾嘅壞蛋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 全丹麥沒一個住在這裡的惡棍,不是個徹頭徹尾的壞蛋。

passages.title: Horatio 霍拉旭
passages.original: There needs no ghost, my lord, come from the grave To tell us this.
passages.vernacular: 殿下,唔需要鬼魂從墳墓出嚟,告訴我哋呢個。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 殿下,不需要鬼魂從墳墓出來,告訴我們這個。

passages.title: Hamlet 哈姆雷特
passages.original: Why, right; you are i’ the right; And so, without more circumstance at all, I hold it fit that we shake hands and part: You, as your business and desire shall point you,— For every man hath business and desire, Such as it is;—and for my own poor part, Look you, I’ll go pray.
passages.vernacular: 係啦,你講得啱;咁就冇更多細節,我認為我哋握手分別最適合:你,按你嘅事務同慾望指引你——因為每個人都有事務同慾望,不管係咩——至於我自己可憐嘅一份,你睇,我去祈禱。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是啊,你說得對;那就沒更多細節,我認為我們握手分別最適合:你,按你的事務和慾望指引你——因為每個人都有事務和慾望,不管是什麼——至於我自己可憐的一份,你看,我去祈禱。

passages.title: Horatio 霍拉旭
passages.original: These are but wild and whirling words, my lord.
passages.vernacular: 呢啲只係狂野旋轉嘅話,殿下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這些只是狂野旋轉的話,殿下。

passages.title: Hamlet 哈姆雷特
passages.original: I’m sorry they offend you, heartily; Yes faith, heartily.
passages.vernacular: 我真心抱歉佢哋冒犯你;係,老實講,真心抱歉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我真心抱歉它們冒犯你;是,老實說,真心抱歉。

passages.title: Horatio 霍拉旭
passages.original: There’s no offence, my lord.
passages.vernacular: 冇冒犯,殿下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒冒犯,殿下。

passages.title: Hamlet 哈姆雷特
passages.original: Yes, by Saint Patrick, but there is, Horatio, And much offence too. Touching this vision here, It is an honest ghost, that let me tell you. For your desire to know what is between us, O’ermaster’t as you may. And now, good friends, As you are friends, scholars, and soldiers, Give me one poor request.
passages.vernacular: 有,憑聖帕特里克,有,霍拉旭,而且好大冒犯。關於呢個景象,佢係一個誠實嘅鬼魂,我告訴你。至於你想知道我哋之間係咩,盡量克制。而家,好朋友,既然你哋係朋友、學者同軍人,畀我一個可憐嘅請求。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有,憑聖帕特里克,有,霍拉旭,而且很大冒犯。關於這個景象,它是一個誠實的鬼魂,我告訴你。至於你想知道我們之間是什麼,盡量克制。現在,好朋友,既然你們是朋友、學者和軍人,給我一個可憐的請求。

passages.title: Horatio 霍拉旭
passages.original: What is’t, my lord? We will.
passages.vernacular: 係咩,殿下?我哋願意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是什麼,殿下?我們願意。

passages.title: Hamlet 哈姆雷特
passages.original: Never make known what you have seen tonight.
passages.vernacular: 永遠唔好公開你哋今晚所見嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 永遠不要公開你們今晚所見的。

passages.title: Horatio And Marcellus 霍拉旭同馬賽勒斯
passages.original: My lord, we will not.
passages.vernacular: 殿下,我哋唔會。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 殿下,我們不會。

passages.title: Hamlet 哈姆雷特
passages.original: Nay, but swear’t.
passages.vernacular: 唔,不過要發誓。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,不過要發誓。

passages.title: Horatio 霍拉旭
passages.original: In faith, my lord, not I.
passages.vernacular: 老實講,殿下,我唔會。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老實說,殿下,我不會。

passages.title: Marcellus 馬賽勒斯
passages.original: Nor I, my lord, in faith.
passages.vernacular: 我亦唔會,殿下,老實講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我也不會,殿下,老實說。

passages.title: Hamlet 哈姆雷特
passages.original: Upon my sword.
passages.vernacular: 憑我嘅劍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 憑我的劍。

passages.title: Marcellus 馬賽勒斯
passages.original: We have sworn, my lord, already.
passages.vernacular: 殿下,我哋已經發過誓。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 殿下,我們已經發過誓。

passages.title: Hamlet 哈姆雷特
passages.original: Indeed, upon my sword, indeed.
passages.vernacular: 確實,憑我嘅劍,確實。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 確實,憑我的劍,確實。

passages.title: Ghost 鬼魂
passages.original: [Cries under the stage.] Swear.
passages.vernacular: [台下喊聲。]發誓。
passages.vernacularMandarin: [台下喊聲。]發誓。

passages.title: Hamlet 哈姆雷特
passages.original: Ha, ha boy, sayst thou so? Art thou there, truepenny? Come on, you hear this fellow in the cellarage. Consent to swear.
passages.vernacular: 哈,哈,孩子,你咁講?你喺嗰度,忠實嘅老友?來,你哋聽到呢個傢伙喺地窖裡。同意發誓。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哈,哈,孩子,你這樣說?你在那裡,忠實的老友?來,你們聽到這個傢伙在地窖裡。同意發誓。

passages.title: Horatio 霍拉旭
passages.original: Propose the oath, my lord.
passages.vernacular: 殿下,提出誓言。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 殿下,提出誓言。

passages.title: Hamlet 哈姆雷特
passages.original: Never to speak of this that you have seen. Swear by my sword.
passages.vernacular: 永遠唔講你哋所見嘅呢件事。憑我嘅劍發誓。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 永遠不說你們所見的這件事。憑我的劍發誓。

passages.title: Ghost 鬼魂
passages.original: [Beneath.] Swear.
passages.vernacular: [在下面。]發誓。
passages.vernacularMandarin: [在下面。]發誓。

passages.title: Hamlet 哈姆雷特
passages.original: Hic et ubique? Then we’ll shift our ground. Come hither, gentlemen, And lay your hands again upon my sword. Never to speak of this that you have heard. Swear by my sword.
passages.vernacular: 到處都係?咁我哋換位置。過嚟,各位,再將你哋嘅手放喺我嘅劍上。永遠唔講你哋所聽到嘅呢件事。憑我嘅劍發誓。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 到處都是?那我們換位置。過來,各位,再將你們的手放在我的劍上。永遠不說你們所聽到的這件事。憑我的劍發誓。

passages.title: Ghost 鬼魂
passages.original: [Beneath.] Swear.
passages.vernacular: [在下面。]發誓。
passages.vernacularMandarin: [在下面。]發誓。

passages.title: Hamlet 哈姆雷特
passages.original: Well said, old mole! Canst work i’ th’earth so fast? A worthy pioner! Once more remove, good friends.
passages.vernacular: 講得好,老鼹鼠!你喺地下可以挖得咁快?一個值得讚賞嘅工兵!再換一次位置,好朋友。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說得好,老鼹鼠!你在地下可以挖得這麼快?一個值得讚賞的工兵!再換一次位置,好朋友。

passages.title: Horatio 霍拉旭
passages.original: O day and night, but this is wondrous strange.
passages.vernacular: 啊日同夜,不過呢件事真係奇怪非常。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊日和夜,不過這件事真是奇怪非常。

passages.title: Hamlet 哈姆雷特
passages.original: And therefore as a stranger give it welcome. There are more things in heaven and earth, Horatio, Than are dreamt of in your philosophy. But come, Here, as before, never, so help you mercy, How strange or odd soe’er I bear myself,— As I perchance hereafter shall think meet To put an antic disposition on— That you, at such times seeing me, never shall, With arms encumber’d thus, or this head-shake, Or by pronouncing of some doubtful phrase, As ‘Well, we know’, or ‘We could and if we would’, Or ‘If we list to speak’; or ‘There be and if they might’, Or such ambiguous giving out, to note That you know aught of me:—this not to do. So grace and mercy at your most need help you, Swear.
passages.vernacular: 所以當佢係陌生人咁歡迎佢。霍拉旭,天上同地上有更多嘢,係你哲學所夢想唔到嘅。不過來,喺呢度,如之前一樣,願慈悲幫你,無論我喺此後可能覺得適合扮出古怪性情時,行為幾咁奇怪或古怪,你哋喺嗰啲時候見到我,永遠唔會,好似咁交叉手臂,或咁搖頭,或者講出某啲含糊嘅話,例如「嗯,我哋知道」,或「如果我哋想,我哋可以」,或「如果我哋願意講」;或「有,如果佢哋可以」,或者咁含糊嘅暗示,去表示你哋知道關於我嘅任何嘢:——唔好咁做。咁願恩典同慈悲在你最需要時幫你,發誓。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以當它是陌生人那樣歡迎它。霍拉旭,天上和地上有更多東西,是你哲學所夢想不到的。不過來,在這裡,如之前一樣,願慈悲幫你,無論我在此後可能覺得適合扮出古怪性情時,行為多奇怪或古怪,你們在那些時候看到我,永遠不會,像這樣交叉手臂,或這樣搖頭,或者說出某些含糊的話,例如「嗯,我們知道」,或「如果我們想,我們可以」,或「如果我們願意說」;或「有,如果他們可以」,或者這樣含糊的暗示,去表示你們知道關於我的任何事:——不要這樣做。那願恩典和慈悲在你最需要時幫你,發誓。

passages.title: Ghost 鬼魂
passages.original: [Beneath.] Swear.
passages.vernacular: [在下面。]發誓。
passages.vernacularMandarin: [在下面。]發誓。

passages.title: Hamlet 哈姆雷特
passages.original: Rest, rest, perturbed spirit. So, gentlemen, With all my love I do commend me to you; And what so poor a man as Hamlet is May do t’express his love and friending to you, God willing, shall not lack. Let us go in together, And still your fingers on your lips, I pray. The time is out of joint. O cursed spite, That ever I was born to set it right. Nay, come, let’s go together.
passages.vernacular: 安息吧,安息吧,不安嘅靈魂。咁,各位,我用我所有嘅愛將我自己託付畀你哋;像哈姆雷特咁可憐嘅人可以用來表達對你哋嘅愛同友誼嘅,願上帝允許,唔會欠缺。我哋一齊入去,請你哋將手指一直放喺嘴唇上。時代脫節喇。啊可咒嘅怨恨,我竟然為咗矯正佢而生!唔,來,我哋一齊去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安息吧,安息吧,不安的靈魂。那麼,各位,我用我所有的愛將我自己託付給你們;像哈姆雷特這麼可憐的人可以用來表達對你們的愛和友誼的,願上帝允許,不會欠缺。我們一起進去,請你們將手指一直放在嘴唇上。時代脫節了。啊可咒的怨恨,我竟然為了矯正它而生!不,來,我們一起去。

passages.original: [Exeunt.]
passages.vernacular: [同下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [同下。]

chapters.title: Act II, Scene I — Polonius’s House 第二幕第一場:波洛涅斯家

passages.original: Enter Polonius and Reynaldo.
passages.vernacular: [波洛涅斯同雷納爾多上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [波洛涅斯和雷納爾多上。]

passages.title: Polonius 波洛涅斯
passages.original: Give him this money and these notes, Reynaldo.
passages.vernacular: 將呢啲錢同呢啲便條交畀佢,雷納爾多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 將這些錢和這些便條交給他,雷納爾多。

passages.title: Reynaldo 雷納爾多
passages.original: I will, my lord.
passages.vernacular: 我會,大人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我會,大人。

passages.title: Polonius 波洛涅斯
passages.original: You shall do marvellous wisely, good Reynaldo, Before you visit him, to make inquiry Of his behaviour.
passages.vernacular: 雷納爾多,你去探望佢之前,先打聽一下佢嘅行為,咁做會非常明智。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雷納爾多,你去探望他之前,先打聽一下他的行為,這樣做會非常明智。

passages.title: Reynaldo 雷納爾多
passages.original: My lord, I did intend it.
passages.vernacular: 大人,我本來就打算咁做。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大人,我本來就打算這樣做。

passages.title: Polonius 波洛涅斯
passages.original: Marry, well said; very well said. Look you, sir, Enquire me first what Danskers are in Paris; And how, and who, what means, and where they keep, What company, at what expense; and finding By this encompassment and drift of question, That they do know my son, come you more nearer Than your particular demands will touch it. Take you as ’twere some distant knowledge of him, As thus, ‘I know his father and his friends, And in part him’—do you mark this, Reynaldo?
passages.vernacular: 對喎,講得好;講得非常好。你聽住,先生,先幫我打聽有咩丹麥人喺巴黎;佢哋點樣、係邊個、有咩財力、住喺邊、結交啲咩人、花費幾多;如果透過呢種迂迴同拐彎抹角嘅發問,發現佢哋認識我個仔,你就比直接盤問更接近問題核心。你要扮作只係對佢有啲遙遠嘅認識,例如咁講:「我認識佢爸爸同佢啲朋友,佢本人就認識少少」——雷納爾多,你留意到嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 對啊,說得好;說得非常好。你聽著,先生,先幫我打聽有哪些丹麥人在巴黎;他們怎樣、是誰、有什麼財力、住在哪、結交些什麼人、花費多少;如果透過這種迂迴和拐彎抹角的發問,發現他們認識我兒子,你就比直接盤問更接近問題核心。你要裝作只是對他有些遙遠的認識,例如這樣說:「我認識他父親和他的朋友,他本人就認識一點」——雷納爾多,你留意到嗎?

passages.title: Reynaldo 雷納爾多
passages.original: Ay, very well, my lord.
passages.vernacular: 留意到,大人,好清楚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 留意到,大人,很清楚。

passages.title: Polonius 波洛涅斯
passages.original: ‘And in part him, but,’ you may say, ‘not well; But if’t be he I mean, he’s very wild; Addicted so and so;’ and there put on him What forgeries you please; marry, none so rank As may dishonour him; take heed of that; But, sir, such wanton, wild, and usual slips As are companions noted and most known To youth and liberty.
passages.vernacular: 「佢本人認識少少,不過」,你可以講,「唔算熟;不過如果我指嘅係佢,佢好放蕩;沉迷呢樣嗰樣」;然後喺嗰度隨你喜歡,加啲編造嘅嘢落佢身上;不過,唔好太惡劣到會玷污佢名譽嗰種;要留意呢點;只係先生,要係啲放縱、狂野、平常嘅過失,即係人所共知、與青春同自由為伴嘅嗰啲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他本人認識一點,不過」,你可以說,「不算熟;不過如果我指的是他,他很放蕩;沉迷這樣那樣」;然後在那裡隨你喜歡,加些編造的事到他身上;不過,不要太惡劣到會玷污他名譽的那種;要留意這點;只是先生,要是些放縱、狂野、平常的過失,即是人所共知、與青春和自由為伴的那些。

passages.title: Reynaldo 雷納爾多
passages.original: As gaming, my lord?
passages.vernacular: 例如賭博,大人?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 例如賭博,大人?

passages.title: Polonius 波洛涅斯
passages.original: Ay, or drinking, fencing, swearing, Quarrelling, drabbing. You may go so far.
passages.vernacular: 係,或者飲酒、擊劍、罵粗口、吵架、嫖妓。你可以講到咁上下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是,或者飲酒、擊劍、罵粗口、吵架、嫖妓。你可以說到這個地步。

passages.title: Reynaldo 雷納爾多
passages.original: My lord, that would dishonour him.
passages.vernacular: 大人,咁會玷污佢嘅名譽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大人,那會玷污他的名譽。

passages.title: Polonius 波洛涅斯
passages.original: Faith no, as you may season it in the charge. You must not put another scandal on him, That he is open to incontinency; That’s not my meaning: but breathe his faults so quaintly That they may seem the taints of liberty; The flash and outbreak of a fiery mind, A savageness in unreclaimed blood, Of general assault.
passages.vernacular: 唔會,老實講,只要你喺指控時加啲調味。你唔可以再加另一樁醜聞落佢身上,話佢縱慾無度;我唔係呢個意思:而係將佢嘅過失巧妙地講出,令佢哋似係自由所染嘅瑕疵;係烈火般心靈嘅閃現同爆發,係未馴服血氣中嘅野性,一種普遍會有嘅衝動。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不會,老實說,只要你在指控時加些調味。你不可以再加另一樁醜聞到他身上,說他縱慾無度;我不是這個意思:而是將他的過失巧妙地說出,使它們像是自由所染的瑕疵;是烈火般心靈的閃現和爆發,是未馴服血氣中的野性,一種普遍會有的衝動。

passages.title: Reynaldo 雷納爾多
passages.original: But my good lord—
passages.vernacular: 不過大人——
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過大人——

passages.title: Polonius 波洛涅斯
passages.original: Wherefore should you do this?
passages.vernacular: 你點解要咁做?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你為什麼要這樣做?

passages.title: Reynaldo 雷納爾多
passages.original: Ay, my lord, I would know that.
passages.vernacular: 係呀,大人,我想知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是啊,大人,我想知道。

passages.title: Polonius 波洛涅斯
passages.original: Marry, sir, here’s my drift, And I believe it is a fetch of warrant. You laying these slight sullies on my son, As ’twere a thing a little soil’d i’ th’ working, Mark you, Your party in converse, him you would sound, Having ever seen in the prenominate crimes The youth you breathe of guilty, be assur’d He closes with you in this consequence; ‘Good sir,’ or so; or ‘friend,’ or ‘gentleman’— According to the phrase or the addition Of man and country.
passages.vernacular: 好,先生,我嘅用意在此,我相信呢係個有根據嘅計策。你將呢啲輕微嘅污點加喺我個仔身上,好似一件喺製作中有少少弄污嘅東西,你留意——你傾緊偈嘅對象,即係你想試探嘅人,如果曾見過你所講嘅青年犯過上述嘅罪行,你可以肯定,佢會咁樣同你接上話:「好先生」之類;或者「朋友」,或者「紳士」——按照人嘅用語同國家稱呼嘅習慣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好,先生,我的用意在此,我相信這是個有根據的計策。你將這些輕微的污點加在我兒子身上,像一件在製作中有點弄污的東西,你留意——你交談的對象,即是你想試探的人,如果曾見過你所說的青年犯過上述的罪行,你可以肯定,他會這樣和你接上話:「好先生」之類;或者「朋友」,或者「紳士」——按照人的用語和國家稱呼的習慣。

passages.title: Reynaldo 雷納爾多
passages.original: Very good, my lord.
passages.vernacular: 好,大人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好,大人。

passages.title: Polonius 波洛涅斯
passages.original: And then, sir, does he this,— He does—What was I about to say? By the mass, I was about to say something. Where did I leave?
passages.vernacular: 然後,先生,佢會咁做——佢會——我本來想講咩?憑彌撒發誓,我本來想講啲嘢。我講到邊?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後,先生,他會這樣做——他會——我本來想說什麼?憑彌撒發誓,我本來想說些什麼。我說到哪?

passages.title: Reynaldo 雷納爾多
passages.original: At ‘closes in the consequence.’ At ‘friend or so,’ and ‘gentleman.’
passages.vernacular: 講到「咁樣接上話」。講到「朋友之類」同「紳士」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說到「這樣接上話」。說到「朋友之類」和「紳士」。

passages.title: Polonius 波洛涅斯
passages.original: At ‘closes in the consequence’ ay, marry! He closes with you thus: ‘I know the gentleman, I saw him yesterday, or t’other day, Or then, or then, with such and such; and, as you say, There was he gaming, there o’ertook in’s rouse, There falling out at tennis’: or perchance, ‘I saw him enter such a house of sale’— Videlicet, a brothel, or so forth. See you now; Your bait of falsehood takes this carp of truth; And thus do we of wisdom and of reach, With windlasses, and with assays of bias, By indirections find directions out. So by my former lecture and advice Shall you my son. You have me, have you not?
passages.vernacular: 講到「咁樣接上話」,啱喇!佢會咁樣接話:「我認識呢位紳士,我琴日見過佢,或者前日,或者嗰陣、嗰陣,同某某人一齊;正如你講,佢喺嗰度賭錢,喺嗰度飲醉被人撞見,喺嗰度打網球時吵架」;或者也許「我見佢走入一間售賣店」——即係妓院之類。你而家睇到喇;你虛假嘅餌,釣到真相呢條鯉魚;我哋呢啲有智慧、有遠見嘅人,就係咁用繞圈同斜擲,以迂迴找出正路。咁你就按我之前嘅教誨同忠告去對付我個仔。你明白我嘅意思,係咪?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說到「這樣接上話」,對了!他會這樣接話:「我認識這位紳士,我昨天見過他,或者前天,或者那時、那時,和某某人一起;正如你說,他在那裡賭錢,在那裡喝醉被人撞見,在那裡打網球時吵架」;或者也許「我見他走進一間售賣店」——即是妓院之類。你現在看到了;你虛假的餌,釣到真相這條鯉魚;我們這些有智慧、有遠見的人,就是這樣用繞圈和斜擲,以迂迴找出正路。那你就按我之前的教誨和忠告去對付我兒子。你明白我的意思,是不是?

passages.title: Reynaldo 雷納爾多
passages.original: My lord, I have.
passages.vernacular: 大人,明白。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大人,明白。

passages.title: Polonius 波洛涅斯
passages.original: God b’ wi’ you, fare you well.
passages.vernacular: 願上帝與你同在,再見。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 願上帝與你同在,再見。

passages.title: Reynaldo 雷納爾多
passages.original: Good my lord.
passages.vernacular: 大人慢行。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大人慢走。

passages.title: Polonius 波洛涅斯
passages.original: Observe his inclination in yourself.
passages.vernacular: 你要親自觀察佢嘅傾向。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你要親自觀察他的傾向。

passages.title: Reynaldo 雷納爾多
passages.original: I shall, my lord.
passages.vernacular: 我會,大人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我會,大人。

passages.title: Polonius 波洛涅斯
passages.original: And let him ply his music.
passages.vernacular: 仲要讓佢繼續練佢嘅音樂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還要讓他繼續練他的音樂。

passages.title: Reynaldo 雷納爾多
passages.original: Well, my lord.
passages.vernacular: 好,大人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好,大人。

passages.title: Polonius 波洛涅斯
passages.original: Farewell.
passages.vernacular: 再見。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 再見。

passages.original: [Exit Reynaldo.]
passages.vernacular: [雷納爾多下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [雷納爾多下。]

passages.original: Enter Ophelia.
passages.vernacular: [奧菲莉亞上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [奧菲莉亞上。]

passages.title: Polonius 波洛涅斯
passages.original: How now, Ophelia, what’s the matter?
passages.vernacular: 點呀,奧菲莉亞,出咗咩事?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 怎麼了,奧菲莉亞,出了什麼事?

passages.title: Ophelia 奧菲莉亞
passages.original: Alas, my lord, I have been so affrighted.
passages.vernacular: 哎呀,大人,我受咗好大驚嚇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哎呀,大人,我受了很大驚嚇。

passages.title: Polonius 波洛涅斯
passages.original: With what, in the name of God?
passages.vernacular: 憑上帝之名,被咩嚇到?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 憑上帝之名,被什麼嚇到?

passages.title: Ophelia 奧菲莉亞
passages.original: My lord, as I was sewing in my chamber, Lord Hamlet, with his doublet all unbrac’d, No hat upon his head, his stockings foul’d, Ungart’red, and down-gyved to his ankle, Pale as his shirt, his knees knocking each other, And with a look so piteous in purport As if he had been loosed out of hell To speak of horrors, he comes before me.
passages.vernacular: 大人,我喺房間縫衫嘅時候,哈姆雷特殿下闖到我面前,外衣完全冇扣,頭上冇戴帽,襪子骯髒,冇繫帶,垂到腳踝,臉色白得似佢件襯衫,兩膝互相碰撞,神情淒慘得似剛從地獄被放出嚟講述恐怖事情咁。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大人,我在房間縫衣服的時候,哈姆雷特殿下闖到我面前,外衣完全沒扣,頭上沒戴帽,襪子骯髒,沒繫帶,垂到腳踝,臉色白得像他的襯衫,兩膝互相碰撞,神情淒慘得像剛從地獄被放出來講述恐怖事情一樣。

passages.title: Polonius 波洛涅斯
passages.original: Mad for thy love?
passages.vernacular: 為你嘅愛而瘋?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為你的愛而瘋?

passages.title: Ophelia 奧菲莉亞
passages.original: My lord, I do not know, but truly I do fear it.
passages.vernacular: 大人,我唔知道,不過講真,我好驚係咁。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大人,我不知道,不過說真的,我很怕是這樣。

passages.title: Polonius 波洛涅斯
passages.original: What said he?
passages.vernacular: 佢講咗啲咩?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他說了些什麼?

passages.title: Ophelia 奧菲莉亞
passages.original: He took me by the wrist and held me hard; Then goes he to the length of all his arm; And with his other hand thus o’er his brow, He falls to such perusal of my face As he would draw it. Long stay’d he so, At last,—a little shaking of mine arm, And thrice his head thus waving up and down, He rais’d a sigh so piteous and profound As it did seem to shatter all his bulk And end his being. That done, he lets me go, And with his head over his shoulder turn’d He seem’d to find his way without his eyes, For out o’ doors he went without their help, And to the last bended their light on me.
passages.vernacular: 佢捉住我手腕,捉得好緊;然後退到佢成條手臂嘅長度;另一隻手就咁放喺額頭上,開始咁仔細打量我嘅臉,好似要將佢畫低咁。佢咁樣停咗好耐,最後——輕輕搖咗搖我嘅手臂,頭上下點咗三次——佢發出一聲咁淒慘咁深沉嘅歎息,好似要震碎佢成個身軀,結束佢嘅生命。之後,佢放開我,頭越過肩膀轉頭,好似唔用眼睛都找到路,因為佢冇靠佢哋幫助就出咗門,到最後仍將佢哋嘅光轉向我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他抓住我手腕,抓得很緊;然後退到他整條手臂的長度;另一隻手就這樣放在額頭上,開始這樣仔細打量我的臉,像要將它畫下來一樣。他這樣停了很久,最後——輕輕搖了搖我的手臂,頭上下點了三次——他發出一聲這麼淒慘這麼深沉的歎息,好像要震碎他整個身軀,結束他的生命。之後,他放開我,頭越過肩膀轉頭,像不用眼睛都找到路,因為他沒靠它們幫助就出了門,到最後仍將它們的光轉向我。

passages.title: Polonius 波洛涅斯
passages.original: Come, go with me. I will go seek the King. This is the very ecstasy of love, Whose violent property fordoes itself, And leads the will to desperate undertakings, As oft as any passion under heaven That does afflict our natures. I am sorry,— What, have you given him any hard words of late?
passages.vernacular: 嚟,跟我嚟。我要去搵國王。呢正係愛嘅狂亂,其暴烈嘅本性會毀滅自己,將意志引向絕望嘅行動,同天底下任何折磨我哋本性嘅激情一樣常咁。我好遺憾——點,你最近有冇對佢講過重話?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來,跟我來。我要去找國王。這正是愛的狂亂,其暴烈的本性會毀滅自己,將意志引向絕望的行動,和天底下任何折磨我們本性的激情一樣常見。我很遺憾——怎麼,你最近有沒有對他說過重話?

passages.title: Ophelia 奧菲莉亞
passages.original: No, my good lord; but as you did command, I did repel his letters and denied His access to me.
passages.vernacular: 冇,大人;不過正如你吩咐,我退回咗佢嘅信,亦拒絕佢嚟見我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有,大人;不過正如你吩咐,我退回了他的信,也拒絕他來見我。

passages.title: Polonius 波洛涅斯
passages.original: That hath made him mad. I am sorry that with better heed and judgement I had not quoted him. I fear’d he did but trifle, And meant to wreck thee. But beshrew my jealousy! It seems it is as proper to our age To cast beyond ourselves in our opinions As it is common for the younger sort To lack discretion. Come, go we to the King. This must be known, which, being kept close, might move More grief to hide than hate to utter love.
passages.vernacular: 咁就令佢發瘋。我後悔自己冇用更好嘅留心同判斷去觀察佢。我驚佢只係玩玩,意圖毀你。不過該死我嘅猜疑!似乎我哋呢個年紀,過分計算、超出自己本分去猜度,正如年輕人常缺乏謹慎一樣平常。嚟,我哋去見國王。呢件事必須讓人知道;收埋佢,可能引致更多悲痛,多過講出愛意招來嘅怨恨。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那就使他發瘋了。我後悔自己沒用更好的留心和判斷去觀察他。我怕他只是玩玩,意圖毀你。不過該死我的猜疑!似乎我們這個年紀,過分計算、超出自己本分去猜度,正如年輕人常缺乏謹慎一樣平常。來,我們去見國王。這件事必須讓人知道;藏起它,可能引致更多悲痛,多過說出愛意招來的怨恨。

passages.original: [Exeunt.]
passages.vernacular: [同下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [同下。]

chapters.title: Act II, Scene II — A Room in the Castle 第二幕第二場:城堡一室

passages.original: Enter King, Queen, Rosencrantz, Guildenstern and Attendants.
passages.vernacular: [國王、王后、羅森克蘭茲、吉爾登斯特恩同侍從上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [國王、王后、羅森克蘭茲、吉爾登斯特恩和侍從上。]

passages.title: King 國王克勞狄斯
passages.original: Welcome, dear Rosencrantz and Guildenstern. Moreover that we much did long to see you, The need we have to use you did provoke Our hasty sending. Something have you heard Of Hamlet’s transformation; so I call it, Since nor th’exterior nor the inward man Resembles that it was. What it should be, More than his father’s death, that thus hath put him So much from th’understanding of himself, I cannot dream of. I entreat you both That, being of so young days brought up with him, And since so neighbour’d to his youth and humour, That you vouchsafe your rest here in our court Some little time, so by your companies To draw him on to pleasures and to gather, So much as from occasion you may glean, Whether aught to us unknown afflicts him thus That, open’d, lies within our remedy.
passages.vernacular: 歡迎,親愛嘅羅森克蘭茲同吉爾登斯特恩。除咗我哋好想見你哋之外,我哋需要借助你哋,亦促使我哋倉促派人去請。你哋大概聽過啲關於哈姆雷特嘅轉變;我咁稱呼佢,因為佢嘅外表同內心都同從前唔一樣。除咗佢爸爸嘅死,究竟係咩令佢咁嚴重失去自我認識,我實在想像唔到。我懇請你哋兩位,既然你哋自細同佢一齊長大,又同佢嘅青春同性情咁接近,請你哋賞面留喺我哋宮廷一段短時間,藉住你哋嘅陪伴引佢享受娛樂,並且盡你哋所能,從機會中探聽,有冇啲我哋唔知道嘅嘢咁折磨住佢,一旦揭開,就喺我哋可補救嘅範圍內。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 歡迎,親愛的羅森克蘭茲和吉爾登斯特恩。除了我們很想見你們之外,我們需要借助你們,也促使我們倉促派人去請。你們大概聽過一些關於哈姆雷特的轉變;我這樣稱呼它,因為他的外表和內心都與從前不一樣。除了他父親的死,究竟是什麼使他這樣嚴重失去自我認識,我實在想像不到。我懇請你們兩位,既然你們自小和他一起長大,又和他的青春和性情這麼接近,請你們賞臉留在我們宮廷一段短時間,藉著你們的陪伴引他享受娛樂,並且盡你們所能,從機會中探聽,有沒有些我們不知道的事這樣折磨著他,一旦揭開,就在我們可補救的範圍內。

passages.title: Queen 王后葛楚德
passages.original: Good gentlemen, he hath much talk’d of you, And sure I am, two men there are not living To whom he more adheres. If it will please you To show us so much gentry and good will As to expend your time with us awhile, For the supply and profit of our hope, Your visitation shall receive such thanks As fits a king’s remembrance.
passages.vernacular: 好先生哋,佢經常提起你哋,我肯定世上冇兩個人比你哋更得佢親近。如果你哋肯賞面,對我哋展現咁多風度同善意,花啲時間陪伴我哋,以補益同滿足我哋嘅期望,你哋嘅到訪會得到配得上君王記掛嘅感謝。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好先生們,他經常提起你們,我肯定世上沒有兩個人比你們更得他親近。如果你們肯賞臉,對我們展現這麼多風度和善意,花些時間陪伴我們,以補益和滿足我們的期望,你們的到訪會得到配得上君王記掛的感謝。

passages.title: Rosencrantz 羅森格蘭茲
passages.original: Both your majesties Might, by the sovereign power you have of us, Put your dread pleasures more into command Than to entreaty.
passages.vernacular: 兩位陛下憑住對我哋擁有嘅至高權力,可以將你哋威嚴嘅意願當作命令,而唔使懇求。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 兩位陛下憑著對我們擁有的至高權力,可以將你們威嚴的意願當作命令,而不用懇求。

passages.title: Guildenstern 吉爾登斯吞
passages.original: We both obey, And here give up ourselves, in the full bent, To lay our service freely at your feet To be commanded.
passages.vernacular: 我哋兩個都服從,並且在此全心奉獻自己,自由地將我哋嘅效勞放喺陛下腳下,聽候差遣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們兩個都服從,並且在此全心奉獻自己,自由地將我們的效勞放在陛下腳下,聽候差遣。

passages.title: King 國王克勞狄斯
passages.original: Thanks, Rosencrantz and gentle Guildenstern.
passages.vernacular: 多謝,羅森克蘭茲同溫文嘅吉爾登斯特恩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 多謝,羅森克蘭茲和溫文的吉爾登斯特恩。

passages.title: Queen 王后葛楚德
passages.original: Thanks, Guildenstern and gentle Rosencrantz. And I beseech you instantly to visit My too much changed son. Go, some of you, And bring these gentlemen where Hamlet is.
passages.vernacular: 多謝,吉爾登斯特恩同溫文嘅羅森克蘭茲。我亦懇請你哋立刻去探望我個變得太多嘅兒子。你哋當中幾個,去帶呢兩位先生去哈姆雷特所在嘅地方。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 多謝,吉爾登斯特恩和溫文的羅森克蘭茲。我也懇請你們立刻去探望我那變得太多的兒子。你們當中幾個,去帶這兩位先生去哈姆雷特所在的地方。

passages.title: Guildenstern 吉爾登斯吞
passages.original: Heavens make our presence and our practices Pleasant and helpful to him.
passages.vernacular: 願上天令我哋嘅出現同行動令佢愉快,對佢有幫助。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 願上天使我們的出現和行動令他愉快,對他有幫助。

passages.title: Queen 王后葛楚德
passages.original: Ay, amen.
passages.vernacular: 係,阿們。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是,阿們。

passages.original: [Exeunt Rosencrantz, Guildenstern and some Attendants.]
passages.vernacular: [羅森克蘭茲、吉爾登斯特恩同幾個侍從下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [羅森克蘭茲、吉爾登斯特恩和幾個侍從下。]

passages.original: Enter Polonius.
passages.vernacular: [波洛涅斯上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [波洛涅斯上。]

passages.title: Polonius 波洛涅斯
passages.original: Th’ambassadors from Norway, my good lord, Are joyfully return’d.
passages.vernacular: 挪威嘅大使,大人,已經歡歡喜喜返嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 挪威的大使,大人,已經歡歡喜喜回來。

passages.title: King 國王克勞狄斯
passages.original: Thou still hast been the father of good news.
passages.vernacular: 你一直都係好消息嘅父親。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你一直都是好消息的父親。

passages.title: Polonius 波洛涅斯
passages.original: Have I, my lord? Assure you, my good liege, I hold my duty, as I hold my soul, Both to my God and to my gracious King: And I do think,—or else this brain of mine Hunts not the trail of policy so sure As it hath us’d to do—that I have found The very cause of Hamlet’s lunacy.
passages.vernacular: 我係嗎,陛下?向陛下保證,我視我嘅責任如同我嘅靈魂,同時對我嘅上帝同仁慈嘅國王負責:而且我認為——否則我呢個腦袋追蹤政治線索,冇似往常咁準——我已經發現咗哈姆雷特發瘋嘅真正原因。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我是嗎,陛下?向陛下保證,我視我的責任如同我的靈魂,同時對我的上帝和仁慈的國王負責:而且我認為——否則我這個腦袋追蹤政治線索,沒有像往常那麼準——我已經發現了哈姆雷特發瘋的真正原因。

passages.title: King 國王克勞狄斯
passages.original: O speak of that, that do I long to hear.
passages.vernacular: 啊,講呢個,我正好想聽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,說這個,我正好想聽。

passages.title: Polonius 波洛涅斯
passages.original: Give first admittance to th’ambassadors; My news shall be the fruit to that great feast.
passages.vernacular: 先接見大使;我嘅消息將係嗰場盛宴嘅甜品。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 先接見大使;我的消息將是那場盛宴的甜品。

passages.title: King 國王克勞狄斯
passages.original: Thyself do grace to them, and bring them in.
passages.vernacular: 你親自招待佢哋,帶佢哋入嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你親自招待他們,帶他們進來。

passages.original: [Exit Polonius.]
passages.vernacular: [波洛涅斯下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [波洛涅斯下。]

passages.title: King 國王克勞狄斯
passages.original: He tells me, my sweet queen, that he hath found The head and source of all your son’s distemper.
passages.vernacular: 親愛嘅王后,佢話我知,佢已經發現你兒子一切失常嘅根源。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 親愛的王后,他告訴我,他已經發現你兒子一切失常的根源。

passages.title: Queen 王后葛楚德
passages.original: I doubt it is no other but the main, His father’s death and our o’erhasty marriage.
passages.vernacular: 我懷疑除咗最主要嗰個,就冇其他,即係佢爸爸嘅死同我哋過急嘅婚事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我懷疑除了最主要的那個,就沒有其他,即是他父親的死和我們過急的婚事。

passages.title: King 國王克勞狄斯
passages.original: Well, we shall sift him.
passages.vernacular: 好,我哋會細細盤問佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好,我們會細細盤問他。

passages.original: Enter Polonius with Voltemand and Cornelius.
passages.vernacular: [波洛涅斯帶沃爾提曼德同科尼利厄斯上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [波洛涅斯帶沃爾提曼德和科尼利厄斯上。]

passages.title: King 國王克勞狄斯
passages.original: Welcome, my good friends! Say, Voltemand, what from our brother Norway?
passages.vernacular: 歡迎,我嘅好朋友!講吧,沃爾提曼德,我哋兄弟挪威國王有咩回覆?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 歡迎,我的好朋友!說吧,沃爾提曼德,我們兄弟挪威國王有什麼回覆?

passages.title: Voltemand 沃爾提曼德
passages.original: Most fair return of greetings and desires. Upon our first, he sent out to suppress His nephew’s levies, which to him appear’d To be a preparation ’gainst the Polack; But better look’d into, he truly found It was against your Highness; whereat griev’d, That so his sickness, age, and impotence Was falsely borne in hand, sends out arrests On Fortinbras; which he, in brief, obeys, Receives rebuke from Norway; and in fine, Makes vow before his uncle never more To give th’assay of arms against your Majesty. Whereon old Norway, overcome with joy, Gives him three thousand crowns in annual fee, And his commission to employ those soldiers So levied as before, against the Polack: With an entreaty, herein further shown, [Gives a paper.] That it might please you to give quiet pass Through your dominions for this enterprise, On such regards of safety and allowance As therein are set down.
passages.vernacular: 最友善嘅問候同心願回覆。一接到我哋第一次要求,佢就派人去制止佢姪子招募軍隊,佢原本以為係為對付波蘭人而做準備;但經過更仔細調查,佢確實發現原來係針對陛下;對此佢深感悲痛,因為佢嘅病弱、年老同無能被人虛假地利用,於是發出逮捕令拘捕福丁布拉斯;佢簡而言之服從,受到挪威嘅責備;最後,當著佢叔叔面前立誓,永不再舉兵對抗陛下。於是老挪威王欣喜若狂,每年畀佢三千克朗年金,並授權佢將之前招募嘅士兵用去對付波蘭人:另附一項請求,於此進一步陳明,[遞上文件。]請陛下恩准,畀佢呢次行動安靜通過陛下嘅領土,條件按文件所列嘅安全同許可而定。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最友善的問候和心願回覆。一接到我們第一次要求,他就派人去制止他姪子招募軍隊,他原本以為是為對付波蘭人而做準備;但經過更仔細調查,他確實發現原來是針對陛下;對此他深感悲痛,因為他的病弱、年老和無能被人虛假地利用,於是發出逮捕令拘捕福丁布拉斯;他簡而言之服從,受到挪威的責備;最後,當著他叔叔面前立誓,永不再舉兵對抗陛下。於是老挪威王欣喜若狂,每年給他三千克朗年金,並授權他將之前招募的士兵用去對付波蘭人:另附一項請求,於此進一步陳明,[遞上文件。]請陛下恩准,讓他這次行動安靜通過陛下的領土,條件按文件所列的安全和許可而定。

passages.title: King 國王克勞狄斯
passages.original: It likes us well; And at our more consider’d time we’ll read, Answer, and think upon this business. Meantime we thank you for your well-took labour. Go to your rest, at night we’ll feast together:. Most welcome home.
passages.vernacular: 我哋好滿意;喺更從容嘅時間,我哋會閱讀、答覆同考慮呢件事。同時多謝你哋辛勤嘅差事。去休息吧,今晚我哋一齊享宴。熱烈歡迎你哋返嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們很滿意;在更從容的時間,我們會閱讀、答覆和考慮這件事。同時多謝你們辛勤的差事。去休息吧,今晚我們一起享宴。熱烈歡迎你們回來。

passages.original: [Exeunt Voltemand and Cornelius.]
passages.vernacular: [沃爾提曼德同科尼利厄斯下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [沃爾提曼德和科尼利厄斯下。]

passages.title: Polonius 波洛涅斯
passages.original: This business is well ended. My liege and madam, to expostulate What majesty should be, what duty is, Why day is day, night night, and time is time Were nothing but to waste night, day and time. Therefore, since brevity is the soul of wit, And tediousness the limbs and outward flourishes, I will be brief. Your noble son is mad. Mad call I it; for to define true madness, What is’t but to be nothing else but mad? But let that go.
passages.vernacular: 呢件事圓滿結束。陛下同娘娘,要論辯君王應該係咩、責任係咩、點解日係日、夜係夜、時間係時間,不過係浪費夜、日同時間。所以,既然簡潔係智慧嘅靈魂,而冗長係四肢同外在嘅點綴,我會簡短。你高貴嘅兒子瘋咗。我稱之為瘋;因為要界定真正嘅瘋狂,除咗瘋,仲有咩?不過算吧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這件事圓滿結束。陛下和娘娘,要論辯君王應該是什麼、責任是什麼、為什麼日是日、夜是夜、時間是時間,不過是浪費夜、日和時間。所以,既然簡潔是智慧的靈魂,而冗長是四肢和外在的點綴,我會簡短。你高貴的兒子瘋了。我稱之為瘋;因為要界定真正的瘋狂,除了瘋,還有什麼?不過算了。

passages.title: Queen 王后葛楚德
passages.original: More matter, with less art.
passages.vernacular: 多啲內容,少啲修辭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 多些內容,少些修辭。

passages.title: Polonius 波洛涅斯
passages.original: Madam, I swear I use no art at all. That he is mad, ’tis true: ’tis true ’tis pity; And pity ’tis ’tis true. A foolish figure, But farewell it, for I will use no art. Mad let us grant him then. And now remains That we find out the cause of this effect, Or rather say, the cause of this defect, For this effect defective comes by cause. Thus it remains, and the remainder thus. Perpend, I have a daughter—have whilst she is mine— Who in her duty and obedience, mark, Hath given me this. Now gather, and surmise. [Reads.] To the celestial, and my soul’s idol, the most beautified Ophelia— That’s an ill phrase, a vile phrase; ‘beautified’ is a vile phrase: but you shall hear. [Reads.] these; in her excellent white bosom, these, &c.
passages.vernacular: 娘娘,我發誓我一啲修辭都冇用。佢瘋咗,係真;真係可惜;可惜嘅係,呢個係真。一個愚蠢嘅修辭,不過就此告別,因為我唔再用修辭。咁我哋就承認佢瘋。而家剩低嘅,就係搵出呢個效果嘅原因,或者應該講,呢個缺陷嘅原因,因為呢個有缺陷嘅效果,必有其因。事情就剩低咁多,而餘下嘅就係咁。請細想,我有一個女兒——只要佢仲係我嘅——佢出於責任同服從,請留意,畀咗我呢個。而家請推敲同推測。[讀。]「獻畀天仙般嘅、我靈魂嘅偶像、最美麗嘅奧菲莉亞——」呢個係個壞用語,一個惡劣嘅用語;「美麗化」係個惡劣嘅用語:不過你哋聽落去。[讀。]呢啲;喺佢優美潔白嘅胸懷中,呢啲,等等。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 娘娘,我發誓我一點修辭都沒用。他瘋了,是真;真是可惜;可惜的是,這是真。一個愚蠢的修辭,不過就此告別,因為我不再用修辭。那我們就承認他瘋。現在剩下的,就是找出這個效果的原因,或者應該說,這個缺陷的原因,因為這個有缺陷的效果,必有其因。事情就剩下這麼多,而餘下的就是這樣。請細想,我有一個女兒——只要她還是我的——她出於責任和服從,請留意,給了我這個。現在請推敲和推測。[讀。]「獻給天仙般的、我靈魂的偶像、最美麗的奧菲莉亞——」這是個壞用語,一個惡劣的用語;「美麗化」是個惡劣的用語:不過你們聽下去。[讀。]這些;在她優美潔白的胸懷中,這些,等等。

passages.title: Queen 王后葛楚德
passages.original: Came this from Hamlet to her?
passages.vernacular: 呢封係哈姆雷特寫畀佢嘅?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這封是哈姆雷特寫給她的?

passages.title: Polonius 波洛涅斯
passages.original: Good madam, stay awhile; I will be faithful. [Reads.] Doubt thou the stars are fire, Doubt that the sun doth move, Doubt truth to be a liar, But never doubt I love. O dear Ophelia, I am ill at these numbers. I have not art to reckon my groans. But that I love thee best, O most best, believe it. Adieu. Thine evermore, most dear lady, whilst this machine is to him, HAMLET. This in obedience hath my daughter show’d me; And more above, hath his solicitings, As they fell out by time, by means, and place, All given to mine ear.
passages.vernacular: 好娘娘,請稍等;我會如實唸出。[讀。]你可以懷疑星星係火,懷疑太陽會移動,懷疑真理係騙子,但永遠唔好懷疑我愛你。啊親愛嘅奧菲莉亞,我唔擅長寫呢啲詩句。我冇本事數算我嘅呻吟。不過我最愛你,啊,最最愛你,請相信。再見。永遠屬於你,最親愛嘅小姐,只要呢副軀體仍屬於佢。哈姆雷特。呢封信,我女兒出於服從,拿畀我睇;而且,佢嘅追求,按時間、方式同地點發生嘅經過,佢都全部講畀我聽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好娘娘,請稍等;我會如實唸出。[讀。]你可以懷疑星星是火,懷疑太陽會移動,懷疑真理是騙子,但永遠不要懷疑我愛你。啊親愛的奧菲莉亞,我不擅長寫這些詩句。我沒本事數算我的呻吟。不過我最愛你,啊,最最愛你,請相信。再見。永遠屬於你,最親愛的小姐,只要這副軀體仍屬於他。哈姆雷特。這封信,我女兒出於服從,拿給我看;而且,他的追求,按時間、方式和地點發生的經過,她都全部說給我聽。

passages.title: King 國王克勞狄斯
passages.original: But how hath she receiv’d his love?
passages.vernacular: 不過佢點樣接受佢嘅愛?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過她怎樣接受他的愛?

passages.title: Polonius 波洛涅斯
passages.original: What do you think of me?
passages.vernacular: 你覺得我係個點樣嘅人?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你覺得我是個怎樣的人?

passages.title: King 國王克勞狄斯
passages.original: As of a man faithful and honourable.
passages.vernacular: 係個忠誠同光明正大嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是個忠誠和光明正大的人。

passages.title: Polonius 波洛涅斯
passages.original: I would fain prove so. But what might you think, When I had seen this hot love on the wing, As I perceiv’d it, I must tell you that, Before my daughter told me, what might you, Or my dear Majesty your queen here, think, If I had play’d the desk or table-book, Or given my heart a winking, mute and dumb, Or look’d upon this love with idle sight, What might you think? No, I went round to work, And my young mistress thus I did bespeak: ‘Lord Hamlet is a prince, out of thy star. This must not be.’ And then I precepts gave her, That she should lock herself from his resort, Admit no messengers, receive no tokens. Which done, she took the fruits of my advice, And he, repulsed,—a short tale to make— Fell into a sadness, then into a fast, Thence to a watch, thence into a weakness, Thence to a lightness, and, by this declension, Into the madness wherein now he raves, And all we wail for.
passages.vernacular: 我願意證明係咁。不過當我見到呢段熾熱嘅愛情展翅,正如我察覺到,我要告訴你,在我女兒話我知之前,你會點諗,或者我親愛嘅王后陛下你會點諗,如果我扮咗書桌或記事簿,或者令我顆心閉眼、沉默、啞口,或者用閒散嘅目光望呢段愛情,你會點諗?不,我繞個圈去處理,對我呢位年輕小姐咁講:「哈姆雷特殿下係王子,超出你嘅星宿。咁係唔得嘅。」然後我吩咐佢,要將自己鎖起,不見佢嚟訪,唔接見使者,唔收信物。佢照做,接受咗我忠告嘅成果,而佢被拒之後——長話短講——墮入悲傷,然後唔食,再然後失眠,再然後虛弱,再然後神志輕浮,就咁一步步沉淪,落入而家佢咆哮嘅瘋狂,亦係我哋所有人哀嘆嘅瘋狂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我願意證明是這樣。不過當我見到這段熾熱的愛情展翅,正如我察覺到,我要告訴你,在我女兒告訴我之前,你會怎麼想,或者我親愛的王后陛下你會怎麼想,如果我裝成了書桌或記事簿,或者使我的心閉眼、沉默、啞口,或者用閒散的目光看這段愛情,你會怎麼想?不,我繞個圈去處理,對我這位年輕小姐這樣說:「哈姆雷特殿下是王子,超出你的星宿。這是不行的。」然後我吩咐她,要將自己鎖起,不見他來訪,不接見使者,不收信物。她照做,接受了我忠告的成果,而他被拒之後——長話短說——墮入悲傷,然後不食,再然後失眠,再然後虛弱,再然後神志輕浮,就這樣一步步沉淪,落入現在他咆哮的瘋狂,也是我們所有人哀嘆的瘋狂。

passages.title: King 國王克勞狄斯
passages.original: Do you think ’tis this?
passages.vernacular: 你覺得係因為呢個?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你覺得是因為這個?

passages.title: Queen 王后葛楚德
passages.original: It may be, very likely.
passages.vernacular: 可能,好有可能。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可能,很有可能。

passages.title: Polonius 波洛涅斯
passages.original: Hath there been such a time, I’d fain know that, That I have positively said ‘’Tis so,’ When it prov’d otherwise?
passages.vernacular: 有冇試過——我想知道——我斬釘截鐵講過「係咁」,結果證明並非咁?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有沒有試過——我想知道——我斬釘截鐵說過「是這樣」,結果證明並非這樣?

passages.title: King 國王克勞狄斯
passages.original: Not that I know.
passages.vernacular: 據我所知冇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 據我所知沒有。

passages.title: Polonius 波洛涅斯
passages.original: Take this from this, if this be otherwise. [Points to his head and shoulder.] If circumstances lead me, I will find Where truth is hid, though it were hid indeed Within the centre.
passages.vernacular: 如果呢個並非咁,就將呢個同呢個分開。[指頭同肩膀。]只要環境引導我,我會搵出真相藏喺邊,即使真係藏喺地心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果這個並非這樣,就將這個和這個分開。[指頭和肩膀。]只要環境引導我,我會找出真相藏在哪,即使真是藏在地心。

passages.title: King 國王克勞狄斯
passages.original: How may we try it further?
passages.vernacular: 我哋點樣進一步試驗?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們怎樣進一步試驗?

passages.title: Polonius 波洛涅斯
passages.original: You know sometimes he walks four hours together Here in the lobby.
passages.vernacular: 你知道佢有時會喺呢度嘅門廊連續行四個鐘頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你知道他有時會在這裡的門廊連續走四個鐘頭。

passages.title: Queen 王后葛楚德
passages.original: So he does indeed.
passages.vernacular: 佢真係咁。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他真是這樣。

passages.title: Polonius 波洛涅斯
passages.original: At such a time I’ll loose my daughter to him. Be you and I behind an arras then, Mark the encounter. If he love her not, And be not from his reason fall’n thereon, Let me be no assistant for a state, But keep a farm and carters.
passages.vernacular: 呢種時候,我會放我女兒去見佢。咁你同我就躲喺掛毯後面,留意佢哋見面。如果佢唔愛佢,亦並非因此而失去理智,咁我就唔配幫手治國,只配養農場同車夫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這種時候,我會放我女兒去見他。那你和我就躲在掛毯後面,留意他們見面。如果他不愛她,也並非因此而失去理智,那我就不配幫手治國,只配養農場和車夫。

passages.title: King 國王克勞狄斯
passages.original: We will try it.
passages.vernacular: 我哋試試。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們試試。

passages.original: Enter Hamlet, reading.
passages.vernacular: [哈姆雷特讀書上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [哈姆雷特讀書上。]

passages.title: Queen 王后葛楚德
passages.original: But look where sadly the poor wretch comes reading.
passages.vernacular: 不過睇,呢個可憐蟲憂愁咁一邊讀書一邊嚟緊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過看,這個可憐蟲憂愁地一邊讀書一邊來了。

passages.title: Polonius 波洛涅斯
passages.original: Away, I do beseech you, both away I’ll board him presently. O, give me leave.
passages.vernacular: 走開,我懇求你哋,兩位都走開;我即刻同佢接洽。啊,請讓我來。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 走開,我懇求你們,兩位都走開;我立刻和他接洽。啊,請讓我來。

passages.original: [Exeunt King, Queen and Attendants.]
passages.vernacular: [國王、王后同侍從下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [國王、王后和侍從下。]

passages.title: Polonius 波洛涅斯
passages.original: How does my good Lord Hamlet?
passages.vernacular: 我嘅好哈姆雷特殿下,你好嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的好哈姆雷特殿下,你好嗎?

passages.title: Hamlet 哈姆雷特
passages.original: Well, God-a-mercy.
passages.vernacular: 好,多謝上帝。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好,多謝上帝。

passages.title: Polonius 波洛涅斯
passages.original: Do you know me, my lord?
passages.vernacular: 殿下,你認得我嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 殿下,你認得我嗎?

passages.title: Hamlet 哈姆雷特
passages.original: Excellent well. You are a fishmonger.
passages.vernacular: 認得好得很。你係個魚販。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 認得好得很。你是個魚販。

passages.title: Polonius 波洛涅斯
passages.original: Not I, my lord.
passages.vernacular: 唔係我,殿下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不是我,殿下。

passages.title: Hamlet 哈姆雷特
passages.original: Then I would you were so honest a man.
passages.vernacular: 咁我希望你係咁誠實嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那我希望你是這麼誠實的人。

passages.title: Polonius 波洛涅斯
passages.original: Honest, my lord?
passages.vernacular: 誠實,殿下?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 誠實,殿下?

passages.title: Hamlet 哈姆雷特
passages.original: Ay sir, to be honest, as this world goes, is to be one man picked out of ten thousand.
passages.vernacular: 係呀先生,喺呢個世界,做個誠實人,就係一萬人中揀出一個。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是啊先生,在這個世界,做個誠實人,就是一萬人中挑出一個。

passages.title: Polonius 波洛涅斯
passages.original: That’s very true, my lord.
passages.vernacular: 好啱,殿下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 很對,殿下。

passages.title: Hamlet 哈姆雷特
passages.original: For if the sun breed maggots in a dead dog, being a good kissing carrion,— Have you a daughter?
passages.vernacular: 因為如果太陽喺一隻死狗身上孕育蛆蟲,佢仍然係一塊值得親吻嘅腐肉——你有冇女兒?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為如果太陽在一隻死狗身上孕育蛆蟲,它仍然是一塊值得親吻的腐肉——你有沒有女兒?

passages.title: Polonius 波洛涅斯
passages.original: I have, my lord.
passages.vernacular: 有,殿下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有,殿下。

passages.title: Hamlet 哈姆雷特
passages.original: Let her not walk i’ th’ sun. Conception is a blessing, but not as your daughter may conceive. Friend, look to’t.
passages.vernacular: 唔好畀佢喺太陽下行。懷孕係一種祝福,不過唔係你女兒可能咁樣懷。朋友,留神啊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不要讓她在太陽下走。懷孕是一種祝福,不過不是你女兒可能那樣懷。朋友,留神啊。

passages.title: Polonius 波洛涅斯
passages.original: How say you by that? [Aside.] Still harping on my daughter. Yet he knew me not at first; he said I was a fishmonger. He is far gone, far gone. And truly in my youth I suffered much extremity for love; very near this. I’ll speak to him again.—What do you read, my lord?
passages.vernacular: 你對此點睇?[旁白。]仲係念念不忘我個女。但佢起初唔認得我;佢話我係魚販。佢病得好深,好深。講真,我年輕時為愛都受過好大苦楚;都幾似呢個。我再同佢講。——殿下,你睇咩?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你對此怎麼看?[旁白。]還是念念不忘我女兒。但他起初不認得我;他說我是魚販。他病得很深,很深。說真的,我年輕時為愛也受過很大苦楚;很像這個。我再和他說。——殿下,你看什麼?

passages.title: Hamlet 哈姆雷特
passages.original: Words, words, words.
passages.vernacular: 字,字,字。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 字,字,字。

passages.title: Polonius 波洛涅斯
passages.original: What is the matter, my lord?
passages.vernacular: 殿下,講嘅係咩事?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 殿下,講的是什麼事?

passages.title: Hamlet 哈姆雷特
passages.original: Between who?
passages.vernacular: 同邊個之間?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在誰之間?

passages.title: Polonius 波洛涅斯
passages.original: I mean the matter that you read, my lord.
passages.vernacular: 我指你睇嘅內容,殿下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我指你看的內容,殿下。

passages.title: Hamlet 哈姆雷特
passages.original: Slanders, sir. For the satirical slave says here that old men have grey beards; that their faces are wrinkled; their eyes purging thick amber and plum-tree gum; and that they have a plentiful lack of wit, together with most weak hams. All which, sir, though I most powerfully and potently believe, yet I hold it not honesty to have it thus set down. For you yourself, sir, should be old as I am, if like a crab you could go backward.
passages.vernacular: 誹謗,先生。因為嗰個諷刺嘅奴才喺度話老人有灰白鬍鬚;佢哋嘅面起皺紋;眼睛流出濃稠嘅琥珀同梅樹膠;而且佢哋極度缺乏智慧,同時膝彎極度軟弱。先生,所有呢啲,雖然我最強烈最有力咁相信,但我認為咁寫低並唔誠實。因為你自己,先生,如果你可以似螃蟹咁向後行,你都會同我一樣老。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 誹謗,先生。因為那個諷刺的奴才在這裡說老人有灰白鬍鬚;他們的臉起皺紋;眼睛流出濃稠的琥珀和梅樹膠;而且他們極度缺乏智慧,同時膝彎極度軟弱。先生,所有這些,雖然我最強烈最有力地相信,但我認為這樣寫下並不誠實。因為你自己,先生,如果你可以像螃蟹那樣向後走,你也會和我一樣老。

passages.title: Polonius 波洛涅斯
passages.original: [Aside.] Though this be madness, yet there is method in’t.— Will you walk out of the air, my lord?
passages.vernacular: [旁白。]雖然呢個係瘋狂,但當中有條理。——殿下,你想唔想入去避下風?
passages.vernacularMandarin: [旁白。]雖然這是瘋狂,但當中有條理。——殿下,你想不想進去避避風?

passages.title: Hamlet 哈姆雷特
passages.original: Into my grave?
passages.vernacular: 入我嘅墳墓?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 進我的墳墓?

passages.title: Polonius 波洛涅斯
passages.original: Indeed, that is out o’ the air. [Aside.] How pregnant sometimes his replies are! A happiness that often madness hits on, which reason and sanity could not so prosperously be delivered of. I will leave him and suddenly contrive the means of meeting between him and my daughter. My honourable lord, I will most humbly take my leave of you.
passages.vernacular: 確實,嗰度係避開空氣嘅。[旁白。]佢有時啲回答幾咁意味深長!呢種妙語,瘋狂經常撞中,而理智同清醒反而未必咁成功地講得出。我而家離開佢,即刻安排佢同我女兒見面嘅辦法。尊貴嘅殿下,我最謙卑地向你告辭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 確實,那裡是避開空氣的。[旁白。]他有時的回答多麼意味深長!這種妙語,瘋狂經常撞中,而理智和清醒反而未必能這樣成功地說出。我現在離開他,立刻安排他和我女兒見面的辦法。尊貴的殿下,我最謙卑地向你告辭。

passages.title: Hamlet 哈姆雷特
passages.original: You cannot, sir, take from me anything that I will more willingly part withal, except my life, except my life, except my life.
passages.vernacular: 先生,你冇乜可以從我身上拿走,比呢個更令我樂意割捨——除咗我條命,除咗我條命,除咗我條命。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 先生,你沒什麼可以從我身上拿走,比這個更使我樂意割捨——除了我的命,除了我的命,除了我的命。

passages.title: Polonius 波洛涅斯
passages.original: Fare you well, my lord.
passages.vernacular: 殿下,再見。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 殿下,再見。

passages.title: Hamlet 哈姆雷特
passages.original: These tedious old fools.
passages.vernacular: 呢啲悶人嘅老傻瓜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這些悶人的老傻瓜。

passages.original: Enter Rosencrantz and Guildenstern.
passages.vernacular: [羅森克蘭茲同吉爾登斯特恩上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [羅森克蘭茲和吉爾登斯特恩上。]

passages.title: Polonius 波洛涅斯
passages.original: You go to seek the Lord Hamlet; there he is.
passages.vernacular: 你哋去搵哈姆雷特殿下;佢喺嗰度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你們去找哈姆雷特殿下;他在那裡。

passages.title: Rosencrantz 羅森格蘭茲
passages.original: [To Polonius.] God save you, sir.
passages.vernacular: [對波洛涅斯。]願上帝保佑你,先生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: [對波洛涅斯。]願上帝保佑你,先生。

passages.original: [Exit Polonius.]
passages.vernacular: [波洛涅斯下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [波洛涅斯下。]

passages.title: Guildenstern 吉爾登斯吞
passages.original: My honoured lord!
passages.vernacular: 尊貴嘅殿下!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 尊貴的殿下!

passages.title: Rosencrantz 羅森格蘭茲
passages.original: My most dear lord!
passages.vernacular: 我最親愛嘅殿下!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我最親愛的殿下!

passages.title: Hamlet 哈姆雷特
passages.original: My excellent good friends! How dost thou, Guildenstern? Ah, Rosencrantz. Good lads, how do ye both?
passages.vernacular: 我最好嘅朋友!吉爾登斯特恩,你好嗎?啊,羅森克蘭茲。好孩子哋,你哋兩個點呀?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我最好的朋友!吉爾登斯特恩,你好嗎?啊,羅森克蘭茲。好孩子們,你們兩個怎樣?

passages.title: Rosencrantz 羅森格蘭茲
passages.original: As the indifferent children of the earth.
passages.vernacular: 好似大地上普通嘅孩子咁。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 像大地上普通的孩子那樣。

passages.title: Guildenstern 吉爾登斯吞
passages.original: Happy in that we are not over-happy; On Fortune’s cap we are not the very button.
passages.vernacular: 慶幸嘅係我哋唔係過分幸運;喺命運之神嘅帽上,我哋唔係頂端嗰粒鈕。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 慶幸的是我們不是過分幸運;在命運之神的帽上,我們不是頂端那顆鈕。

passages.title: Hamlet 哈姆雷特
passages.original: Nor the soles of her shoe?
passages.vernacular: 亦唔係佢鞋底?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 也不是她鞋底?

passages.title: Rosencrantz 羅森格蘭茲
passages.original: Neither, my lord.
passages.vernacular: 都唔係,殿下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 都不是,殿下。

passages.title: Hamlet 哈姆雷特
passages.original: Then you live about her waist, or in the middle of her favours?
passages.vernacular: 咁你哋住喺佢腰間,或者佢恩寵嘅中間?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那你們住在她腰間,或者她恩寵的中間?

passages.title: Guildenstern 吉爾登斯吞
passages.original: Faith, her privates we.
passages.vernacular: 講真,我哋係佢嘅私處。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說真的,我們是她的私處。

passages.title: Hamlet 哈姆雷特
passages.original: In the secret parts of Fortune? O, most true; she is a strumpet. What’s the news?
passages.vernacular: 喺命運之神嘅隱秘部位?啊,最真;佢係個娼婦。有咩消息?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在命運之神的隱祕部位?啊,最真;她是個娼婦。有什麼消息?

passages.title: Rosencrantz 羅森格蘭茲
passages.original: None, my lord, but that the world’s grown honest.
passages.vernacular: 冇,殿下,除咗世界變得誠實。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有,殿下,除了世界變得誠實。

passages.title: Hamlet 哈姆雷特
passages.original: Then is doomsday near. But your news is not true. Let me question more in particular. What have you, my good friends, deserved at the hands of Fortune, that she sends you to prison hither?
passages.vernacular: 咁末日就近喇。不過你嘅消息並不真。讓我問得更具體。我嘅好朋友,你哋對命運之神做咗啲咩,令佢送你哋嚟呢度坐牢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那末日就近了。不過你的消息並不真。讓我問得更具體。我的好朋友,你們對命運之神做了些什麼,使她送你們來這裡坐牢?

passages.title: Guildenstern 吉爾登斯吞
passages.original: Prison, my lord?
passages.vernacular: 坐牢,殿下?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 坐牢,殿下?

passages.title: Hamlet 哈姆雷特
passages.original: Denmark’s a prison.
passages.vernacular: 丹麥係座監獄。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 丹麥是座監獄。

passages.title: Rosencrantz 羅森格蘭茲
passages.original: Then is the world one.
passages.vernacular: 咁世界就係一座。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那世界就是一座。

passages.title: Hamlet 哈姆雷特
passages.original: A goodly one; in which there are many confines, wards, and dungeons, Denmark being one o’ th’ worst.
passages.vernacular: 一座好大嘅監獄;裡面有好多監禁室、牢房同地牢,丹麥係最差嘅其中之一。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一座很大的監獄;裡面有很多監禁室、牢房和地牢,丹麥是最差的其中之一。

passages.title: Rosencrantz 羅森格蘭茲
passages.original: We think not so, my lord.
passages.vernacular: 我哋唔咁認為,殿下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們不這樣認為,殿下。

passages.title: Hamlet 哈姆雷特
passages.original: Why, then ’tis none to you; for there is nothing either good or bad but thinking makes it so. To me it is a prison.
passages.vernacular: 咁對你哋就唔係;因為世上冇嘢本質上好或壞,係思想令佢咁。對我嚟講佢係座監獄。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那對你們就不是;因為世上沒有東西本質上好或壞,是思想使它這樣。對我來說它是座監獄。

passages.title: Rosencrantz 羅森格蘭茲
passages.original: Why, then your ambition makes it one; ’tis too narrow for your mind.
passages.vernacular: 咁係你嘅野心令佢成為監獄;佢對你嘅心靈嚟講太窄。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是你的野心使它成為監獄;它對你的心靈來說太窄。

passages.title: Hamlet 哈姆雷特
passages.original: O God, I could be bounded in a nutshell, and count myself a king of infinite space, were it not that I have bad dreams.
passages.vernacular: 啊上帝,我可以被困喺一個果殼之中,仍視自己為無限空間之王,只要我冇做惡夢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊上帝,我可以被困在一個果殼之中,仍視自己為無限空間之王,只要我沒做惡夢。

passages.title: Guildenstern 吉爾登斯吞
passages.original: Which dreams, indeed, are ambition; for the very substance of the ambitious is merely the shadow of a dream.
passages.vernacular: 而呢啲夢確實就係野心;因為野心家嘅實質,不過係一個夢嘅影子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而這些夢確實就是野心;因為野心家的實質,不過是一個夢的影子。

passages.title: Hamlet 哈姆雷特
passages.original: A dream itself is but a shadow.
passages.vernacular: 夢本身只不過係個影子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 夢本身只不過是個影子。

passages.title: Rosencrantz 羅森格蘭茲
passages.original: Truly, and I hold ambition of so airy and light a quality that it is but a shadow’s shadow.
passages.vernacular: 確實,我認為野心係咁輕盈虛無,以致佢只係影子嘅影子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 確實,我認為野心是這樣輕盈虛無,以致它只是影子的影子。

passages.title: Hamlet 哈姆雷特
passages.original: Then are our beggars bodies, and our monarchs and outstretch’d heroes the beggars’ shadows. Shall we to th’ court? For, by my fay, I cannot reason.
passages.vernacular: 咁我哋嘅乞丐就係實體,而我哋嘅君王同伸展肢體嘅英雄,就係乞丐嘅影子。我哋入宮好嗎?因為憑我嘅信義,我無法推理。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那我們的乞丐就是實體,而我們的君王和伸展肢體的英雄,就是乞丐的影子。我們進宮好嗎?因為憑我的信義,我無法推理。

passages.title: Rosencrantz And Guildenstern 羅森格蘭茲同吉爾登斯吞
passages.original: We’ll wait upon you.
passages.vernacular: 我哋聽候你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們聽候你。

passages.title: Hamlet 哈姆雷特
passages.original: No such matter. I will not sort you with the rest of my servants; for, to speak to you like an honest man, I am most dreadfully attended. But, in the beaten way of friendship, what make you at Elsinore?
passages.vernacular: 唔使咁。我唔會將你哋同我其他僕人歸為一類;因為,同你哋老實講,我身邊嘅隨從可怕到極點。不過,按朋友之間慣常嘅方式,你哋嚟艾爾西諾做咩?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不用這樣。我不會將你們和我其他僕人歸為一類;因為,和你們老實說,我身邊的隨從可怕到極點。不過,按朋友之間慣常的方式,你們來艾爾西諾做什麼?

passages.title: Rosencrantz 羅森格蘭茲
passages.original: To visit you, my lord, no other occasion.
passages.vernacular: 探望你,殿下,冇其他原因。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 探望你,殿下,沒其他原因。

passages.title: Hamlet 哈姆雷特
passages.original: Beggar that I am, I am even poor in thanks; but I thank you. And sure, dear friends, my thanks are too dear a halfpenny. Were you not sent for? Is it your own inclining? Is it a free visitation? Come, deal justly with me. Come, come; nay, speak.
passages.vernacular: 我呢個乞丐,連感謝都貧乏;不過我多謝你哋。而且肯定,親愛嘅朋友,我嘅感謝,就算半個便士都嫌太貴。你哋唔係被人召嚟嗎?係你哋自己想嚟?係自由嘅探訪?嚟,對我公道啲。嚟嚟;講啦。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我這個乞丐,連感謝都貧乏;不過我多謝你們。而且肯定,親愛的朋友,我的感謝,就算半個便士都嫌太貴。你們不是被人召來嗎?是你們自己想來?是自由的探訪?來,對我公道些。來來;說吧。

passages.title: Guildenstern 吉爾登斯吞
passages.original: What should we say, my lord?
passages.vernacular: 我哋應該講咩,殿下?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們應該說什麼,殿下?

passages.title: Hamlet 哈姆雷特
passages.original: Why, anything. But to the purpose. You were sent for; and there is a kind of confession in your looks, which your modesties have not craft enough to colour. I know the good King and Queen have sent for you.
passages.vernacular: 講咩都得。不過要切題。你哋係被召嚟嘅;你哋嘅神情有一種招認,你哋嘅謙遜冇足夠技巧去掩飾。我知道好國王同王后召你哋嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說什麼都行。不過要切題。你們是被召來的;你們的神情有一種招認,你們的謙遜沒足夠技巧去掩飾。我知道好國王和王后召你們來。

passages.title: Rosencrantz 羅森格蘭茲
passages.original: To what end, my lord?
passages.vernacular: 為咗咩目的,殿下?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為了什麼目的,殿下?

passages.title: Hamlet 哈姆雷特
passages.original: That you must teach me. But let me conjure you, by the rights of our fellowship, by the consonancy of our youth, by the obligation of our ever-preserved love, and by what more dear a better proposer could charge you withal, be even and direct with me, whether you were sent for or no.
passages.vernacular: 呢個要由你哋教我。不過讓我以我哋友誼嘅權利、我哋青春嘅和諧、我哋永遠保存嘅愛嘅義務,以及一個更好嘅提問者可以用來責成你哋嘅更親切嘅理由,懇求你哋,坦率直接對我講,你哋係咪被召嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這個要由你們教我。不過讓我以我們友誼的權利、我們青春的和諧、我們永遠保存的愛的義務,以及一個更好的提問者可以用來責成你們的更親切的理由,懇求你們,坦率直接對我說,你們是不是被召來。

passages.title: Rosencrantz 羅森格蘭茲
passages.original: [To Guildenstern.] What say you?
passages.vernacular: [對吉爾登斯特恩。]你點講?
passages.vernacularMandarin: [對吉爾登斯特恩。]你怎麼說?

passages.title: Hamlet 哈姆雷特
passages.original: [Aside.] Nay, then I have an eye of you. If you love me, hold not off.
passages.vernacular: [旁白。]唔,咁我睇穿你哋。如果你哋愛我,就唔好閃躲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: [旁白。]不,那我看穿你們。如果你們愛我,就不要閃躲。

passages.title: Guildenstern 吉爾登斯吞
passages.original: My lord, we were sent for.
passages.vernacular: 殿下,我哋係被召嚟嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 殿下,我們是被召來的。

passages.title: Hamlet 哈姆雷特
passages.original: I will tell you why; so shall my anticipation prevent your discovery, and your secrecy to the King and Queen moult no feather. I have of late, but wherefore I know not, lost all my mirth, forgone all custom of exercises; and indeed, it goes so heavily with my disposition that this goodly frame the earth, seems to me a sterile promontory; this most excellent canopy the air, look you, this brave o’erhanging firmament, this majestical roof fretted with golden fire, why, it appears no other thing to me than a foul and pestilent congregation of vapours. What a piece of work is man, how noble in reason, how infinite in faculties, in form and moving, how express and admirable; in action how like an angel, in apprehension, how like a god: the beauty of the world, the paragon of animals. And yet, to me, what is this quintessence of dust? Man delights not me; no, nor woman neither, though by your smiling you seem to say so.
passages.vernacular: 我話你知點解;咁我嘅先講,就會預先阻止你哋嘅坦白,而你哋對國王同王后嘅保密亦唔會掉半根羽毛。近來,我唔知點解,失去咗所有歡樂,放棄咗所有日常運動;確實,我心情沉重到,呢個美好嘅大地對我嚟講,似一個貧瘠嘅岬角;呢個最出色嘅華蓋,空氣,你睇,呢個壯麗嘅懸空穹蒼,呢個鑲滿金色火焰嘅莊嚴屋頂,唔,對我嚟講,佢只不過係一堆污穢有害嘅蒸氣。人類真係一件傑作!理性多高貴,能力多無窮,形態同動作多精確多可敬;行動上多似天使,領悟上多似神明:世界嘅美,萬物之靈長。然而,對我嚟講,呢個塵土精華算係咩?人類唔令我喜悅;唔,女人亦唔,雖然你哋笑,似係話係咁。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我告訴你為什麼;這樣我的先說,就會預先阻止你們的坦白,而你們對國王和王后的保密也不會掉半根羽毛。近來,我不知為什麼,失去了所有歡樂,放棄了所有日常運動;確實,我心情沉重到,這個美好的大地對我來說,像一個貧瘠的岬角;這個最出色的華蓋,空氣,你看,這個壯麗的懸空穹蒼,這個鑲滿金色火焰的莊嚴屋頂,不,對我來說,它只不過是一堆污穢有害的蒸氣。人類真是一件傑作!理性多高貴,能力多無窮,形態和動作多精確多可敬;行動上多像天使,領悟上多像神明:世界的美,萬物之靈長。然而,對我來說,這個塵土精華算是什麼?人類不使我喜悅;不,女人也不,雖然你們笑,像是說是這樣。

passages.title: Rosencrantz 羅森格蘭茲
passages.original: My lord, there was no such stuff in my thoughts.
passages.vernacular: 殿下,我心裡冇呢啲嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 殿下,我心裡沒這些念頭。

passages.title: Hamlet 哈姆雷特
passages.original: Why did you laugh then, when I said ‘Man delights not me’?
passages.vernacular: 咁你點解笑,當我話「人類唔令我喜悅」?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那你為什麼笑,當我說「人類不使我喜悅」?

passages.title: Rosencrantz 羅森格蘭茲
passages.original: To think, my lord, if you delight not in man, what Lenten entertainment the players shall receive from you. We coted them on the way, and hither are they coming to offer you service.
passages.vernacular: 我想,殿下,如果你唔喜歡人類,咁啲演員會從你得到幾淡薄嘅款待。我哋喺途中趕過佢哋,佢哋而家嚟緊呢度,向你獻藝。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想,殿下,如果你不喜歡人類,那些演員會從你得到多淡薄的款待。我們在途中趕過他們,他們現在正來這裡,向你獻藝。

passages.title: Hamlet 哈姆雷特
passages.original: He that plays the king shall be welcome,—his Majesty shall have tribute of me; the adventurous knight shall use his foil and target; the lover shall not sigh gratis, the humorous man shall end his part in peace; the clown shall make those laugh whose lungs are tickle o’ th’ sere; and the lady shall say her mind freely, or the blank verse shall halt for’t. What players are they?
passages.vernacular: 扮國王嗰個會受歡迎——陛下會從我得到貢品;冒險騎士會用佢嘅鈍劍同盾牌;情人唔會白白歎息,脾氣古怪嘅人會平靜結束佢嘅角色;小丑會令啲一觸即笑嘅肺部發笑;而女士會自由講出佢嘅心意,否則無韻詩會為此跛行。係啲咩演員?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 扮國王的那個會受歡迎——陛下會從我得到貢品;冒險騎士會用他的鈍劍和盾牌;情人不會白白歎息,脾氣古怪的人會平靜結束他的角色;小丑會使那些一觸即笑的肺部發笑;而女士會自由說出她的心意,否則無韻詩會為此跛行。是些什麼演員?

passages.title: Rosencrantz 羅森格蘭茲
passages.original: Even those you were wont to take such delight in—the tragedians of the city.
passages.vernacular: 正係你一向咁喜愛嘅嗰班——城裡嘅悲劇演員。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 正是你一向這麼喜愛的那班——城裡的悲劇演員。

passages.title: Hamlet 哈姆雷特
passages.original: How chances it they travel? Their residence, both in reputation and profit, was better both ways.
passages.vernacular: 點解佢哋要巡迴?佢哋留喺城裡,無論名聲定收益,兩方面都更好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為什麼他們要巡迴?他們留在城裡,無論名聲還是收益,兩方面都更好。

passages.title: Rosencrantz 羅森格蘭茲
passages.original: I think their inhibition comes by the means of the late innovation.
passages.vernacular: 我想佢哋被禁係因為最近嘅革新。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想他們被禁是因為最近的革新。

passages.title: Hamlet 哈姆雷特
passages.original: Do they hold the same estimation they did when I was in the city? Are they so followed?
passages.vernacular: 佢哋仲係同我喺城時一樣受重視嗎?仲係咁多人追捧?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們還是和我在城裡時一樣受重視嗎?還是這麼多人追捧?

passages.title: Rosencrantz 羅森格蘭茲
passages.original: No, indeed, they are not.
passages.vernacular: 唔,確實唔係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,確實不是。

passages.title: Hamlet 哈姆雷特
passages.original: How comes it? Do they grow rusty?
passages.vernacular: 點解?佢哋生鏽咗?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為什麼?他們生鏽了?

passages.title: Rosencrantz 羅森格蘭茲
passages.original: Nay, their endeavour keeps in the wonted pace; but there is, sir, an aerie of children, little eyases, that cry out on the top of question, and are most tyrannically clapped for’t. These are now the fashion, and so berattle the common stages—so they call them—that many wearing rapiers are afraid of goose-quills and dare scarce come thither.
passages.vernacular: 唔,佢哋嘅努力維持住慣常步伐;不過先生,有一窩小孩,小鷹仔,響亮喊叫,聲浪壓過台詞,而且為此被極度專橫地鼓掌。呢啲而家流行,並且將普通戲台——佢哋咁稱呼——吵得震天響,令好多佩劍嘅人驚鵝毛筆,幾乎唔敢去嗰度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,他們的努力維持著慣常步伐;不過先生,有一窩小孩,小鷹仔,響亮喊叫,聲浪壓過台詞,而且為此被極度專橫地鼓掌。這些現在流行,並且將普通戲台——他們這樣稱呼——吵得震天響,使很多佩劍的人怕鵝毛筆,幾乎不敢去那裡。

passages.title: Hamlet 哈姆雷特
passages.original: What, are they children? Who maintains ’em? How are they escoted? Will they pursue the quality no longer than they can sing? Will they not say afterwards, if they should grow themselves to common players—as it is most like, if their means are no better—their writers do them wrong to make them exclaim against their own succession?
passages.vernacular: 咩,佢哋係小孩?邊個養佢哋?佢哋靠咩支付費用?佢哋追求呢個行業,只會到變聲為止?如果佢哋長大成為普通演員——好有可能,如果佢哋嘅財力冇更好——佢哋之後唔會話,佢哋嘅編劇對佢哋唔公平,令佢哋呼喊攻擊自己將來嘅職業?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 什麼,他們是小孩?誰養他們?他們靠什麼支付費用?他們追求這個行業,只會到變聲為止?如果他們長大成為普通演員——很有可能,如果他們的財力沒有更好——他們之後不會說,他們的編劇對他們不公平,使他們呼喊攻擊自己將來的職業?

passages.title: Rosencrantz 羅森格蘭茲
passages.original: Faith, there has been much to do on both sides; and the nation holds it no sin to tarre them to controversy. There was for a while, no money bid for argument unless the poet and the player went to cuffs in the question.
passages.vernacular: 老實講,雙方都鬧得好厲害;全國都唔認為煽動佢哋爭論有罪。有一陣子,除非詩人同演員喺爭論中動手,否則劇本賣唔到錢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老實說,雙方都鬧得很厲害;全國都不認為煽動他們爭論有罪。有一陣子,除非詩人和演員在爭論中動手,否則劇本賣不到錢。

passages.title: Hamlet 哈姆雷特
passages.original: Is’t possible?
passages.vernacular: 有可能嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有可能嗎?

passages.title: Guildenstern 吉爾登斯吞
passages.original: O, there has been much throwing about of brains.
passages.vernacular: 啊,好多腦袋被拋來拋去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,很多腦袋被拋來拋去。

passages.title: Hamlet 哈姆雷特
passages.original: Do the boys carry it away?
passages.vernacular: 小孩贏咗?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 小孩贏了?

passages.title: Rosencrantz 羅森格蘭茲
passages.original: Ay, that they do, my lord. Hercules and his load too.
passages.vernacular: 係,佢哋贏咗,殿下。連大力神赫拉克勒斯同佢背負嘅地球都贏埋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是,他們贏了,殿下。連大力神赫拉克勒斯和他背負的地球都贏了。

passages.title: Hamlet 哈姆雷特
passages.original: It is not very strange; for my uncle is King of Denmark, and those that would make mouths at him while my father lived, give twenty, forty, fifty, a hundred ducats apiece for his picture in little. ’Sblood, there is something in this more than natural, if philosophy could find it out.
passages.vernacular: 唔算好奇怪;因為我叔叔係丹麥國王,而啲喺我父親在世時對佢扮鬼臉嘅人,而家為佢嘅小畫像肯出二十、四十、五十、一百個杜卡特。天啊,呢件事當中有啲超乎自然嘅嘢,如果哲學能夠搵得出。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不算很奇怪;因為我叔叔是丹麥國王,而那些在我父親在世時對他扮鬼臉的人,現在為他的小畫像肯出二十、四十、五十、一百個杜卡特。天啊,這件事當中有些超乎自然的東西,如果哲學能夠找得出。

passages.original: [Flourish of trumpets within.]
passages.vernacular: [內有號角聲。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [內有號角聲。]

passages.title: Guildenstern 吉爾登斯吞
passages.original: There are the players.
passages.vernacular: 演員到喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 演員到了。

passages.title: Hamlet 哈姆雷特
passages.original: Gentlemen, you are welcome to Elsinore. Your hands, come. The appurtenance of welcome is fashion and ceremony. Let me comply with you in this garb, lest my extent to the players, which I tell you must show fairly outward, should more appear like entertainment than yours. You are welcome. But my uncle-father and aunt-mother are deceived.
passages.vernacular: 先生哋,歡迎你哋嚟艾爾西諾。你哋嘅手,嚟。歡迎嘅附屬品係禮節同儀式。讓我以呢種姿態同你哋客套,免得我對演員嘅招待——我告訴你,必須表面上顯得周到——比對你哋顯得更似款待。歡迎你哋。不過我嘅叔叔爸爸同嬸嬸媽媽被騙咗。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 先生們,歡迎你們來艾爾西諾。你們的手,來。歡迎的附屬品是禮節和儀式。讓我以這種姿態和你們客套,免得我對演員的招待——我告訴你,必須表面上顯得周到——比對你們顯得更像款待。歡迎你們。不過我的叔叔父親和嬸嬸母親被騙了。

passages.title: Guildenstern 吉爾登斯吞
passages.original: In what, my dear lord?
passages.vernacular: 被騙咩,親愛嘅殿下?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 被騙什麼,親愛的殿下?

passages.title: Hamlet 哈姆雷特
passages.original: I am but mad north-north-west. When the wind is southerly, I know a hawk from a handsaw.
passages.vernacular: 我只係西北偏北方向瘋。當吹南風,我分得清老鷹同手鋸。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我只是西北偏北方向瘋。當吹南風,我分得清老鷹和手鋸。

passages.original: Enter Polonius.
passages.vernacular: [波洛涅斯上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [波洛涅斯上。]

passages.title: Polonius 波洛涅斯
passages.original: Well be with you, gentlemen.
passages.vernacular: 願你哋安好,先生哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 願你們安好,先生們。

passages.title: Hamlet 哈姆雷特
passages.original: Hark you, Guildenstern, and you too, at each ear a hearer. That great baby you see there is not yet out of his swaddling clouts.
passages.vernacular: 聽住,吉爾登斯特恩,你亦一樣,每隻耳朵一個聽眾。你睇到嗰個大嬰兒,仲未脫離佢嘅襁褓。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 聽著,吉爾登斯特恩,你也一樣,每隻耳朵一個聽眾。你看到的那個大嬰兒,還未脫離他的襁褓。

passages.title: Rosencrantz 羅森格蘭茲
passages.original: Happily he’s the second time come to them; for they say an old man is twice a child.
passages.vernacular: 或者佢第二次返回襁褓;因為人話老人係第二次做小孩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 或許他第二次回到襁褓;因為人說老人是第二次做小孩。

passages.title: Hamlet 哈姆雷特
passages.original: I will prophesy he comes to tell me of the players. Mark it.—You say right, sir: for a Monday morning ’twas so indeed.
passages.vernacular: 我預言佢係嚟告訴我演員嘅事。留意。——你講得啱,先生:星期一早上確實係咁。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我預言他是來告訴我演員的事。留意。——你說得對,先生:星期一早上確實是這樣。

passages.title: Polonius 波洛涅斯
passages.original: My lord, I have news to tell you.
passages.vernacular: 殿下,我有消息要告訴你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 殿下,我有消息要告訴你。

passages.title: Hamlet 哈姆雷特
passages.original: My lord, I have news to tell you. When Roscius was an actor in Rome—
passages.vernacular: 殿下,我有消息要告訴你。羅修斯在羅馬做演員時——
passages.vernacularMandarin: 殿下,我有消息要告訴你。羅修斯在羅馬做演員時——

passages.title: Polonius 波洛涅斯
passages.original: The actors are come hither, my lord.
passages.vernacular: 演員已經來到此地,殿下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 演員已經來到此地,殿下。

passages.title: Hamlet 哈姆雷特
passages.original: Buzz, buzz.
passages.vernacular: 嗡嗡,嗡嗡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嗡嗡,嗡嗡。

passages.title: Polonius 波洛涅斯
passages.original: Upon my honour.
passages.vernacular: 憑我嘅名譽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 憑我的名譽。

passages.title: Hamlet 哈姆雷特
passages.original: Then came each actor on his ass—
passages.vernacular: 然後每位演員騎住佢嘅驢子嚟——
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後每位演員騎著他的驢子來——

passages.title: Polonius 波洛涅斯
passages.original: The best actors in the world, either for tragedy, comedy, history, pastoral, pastoral-comical, historical-pastoral, tragical-historical, tragical-comical-historical-pastoral, scene individable, or poem unlimited. Seneca cannot be too heavy, nor Plautus too light, for the law of writ and the liberty. These are the only men.
passages.vernacular: 世上最好嘅演員,無論悲劇、喜劇、歷史劇、田園劇、田園喜劇、歷史田園劇、悲劇歷史劇、悲劇喜劇歷史田園劇、不可分場景嘅戲,或者不受限制嘅詩劇。塞內加唔會太沉重,普勞圖斯唔會太輕,不論按劇本規矩抑或自由發揮。呢班就係唯一嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 世上最好的演員,無論悲劇、喜劇、歷史劇、田園劇、田園喜劇、歷史田園劇、悲劇歷史劇、悲劇喜劇歷史田園劇、不可分場景的戲,或者不受限制的詩劇。塞內加不會太沉重,普勞圖斯不會太輕,不論按劇本規矩還是自由發揮。這班就是唯一的人。

passages.title: Hamlet 哈姆雷特
passages.original: O Jephthah, judge of Israel, what a treasure hadst thou!
passages.vernacular: 啊以色列士師耶弗他,你有幾大嘅寶藏!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊以色列士師耶弗他,你有多大的寶藏!

passages.title: Polonius 波洛涅斯
passages.original: What treasure had he, my lord?
passages.vernacular: 佢有咩寶藏,殿下?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他有什麼寶藏,殿下?

passages.title: Hamlet 哈姆雷特
passages.original: Why— ’One fair daughter, and no more, The which he loved passing well.’
passages.vernacular: 咦——「一個美麗女兒,再無其他,佢好疼愛佢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 咦——「一個美麗女兒,再無其他,他非常疼愛她。」

passages.title: Polonius 波洛涅斯
passages.original: [Aside.] Still on my daughter.
passages.vernacular: [旁白。]仲係講我女兒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: [旁白。]還是說我女兒。

passages.title: Hamlet 哈姆雷特
passages.original: Am I not i’ th’ right, old Jephthah?
passages.vernacular: 老耶弗他,我講得啱嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老耶弗他,我說得對嗎?

passages.title: Polonius 波洛涅斯
passages.original: If you call me Jephthah, my lord, I have a daughter that I love passing well.
passages.vernacular: 如果你叫我耶弗他,殿下,我有一個我疼愛得很嘅女兒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你叫我耶弗他,殿下,我有一個我疼愛得很的女兒。

passages.title: Hamlet 哈姆雷特
passages.original: Nay, that follows not.
passages.vernacular: 唔,呢個唔係順理成章。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,這個不是順理成章。

passages.title: Polonius 波洛涅斯
passages.original: What follows then, my lord?
passages.vernacular: 咁接落去係咩,殿下?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那接下來是什麼,殿下?

passages.title: Hamlet 哈姆雷特
passages.original: Why, As by lot, God wot, and then, you know, It came to pass, as most like it was. The first row of the pious chanson will show you more. For look where my abridgement comes.
passages.vernacular: 咦,「如抽籤,上帝知,然後,你知,事情發生喇,最似就係咁」。虔誠歌謠嘅第一行會告訴你更多。因為睇,我嘅「縮略」嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 咦,「如抽籤,上帝知,然後,你知,事情發生了,最像就是這樣」。虔誠歌謠的第一行會告訴你更多。因為看,我的「縮略」來了。

passages.original: Enter four or five Players.
passages.vernacular: [四五個演員上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [四五個演員上。]

passages.title: Hamlet 哈姆雷特
passages.original: You are welcome, masters, welcome all. I am glad to see thee well. Welcome, good friends. O, my old friend! Thy face is valanc’d since I saw thee last. Com’st thou to beard me in Denmark? What, my young lady and mistress! By’r lady, your ladyship is nearer to heaven than when I saw you last, by the altitude of a chopine. Pray God your voice, like a piece of uncurrent gold, be not cracked within the ring. Masters, you are all welcome. We’ll e’en to’t like French falconers, fly at anything we see. We’ll have a speech straight. Come, give us a taste of your quality. Come, a passionate speech.
passages.vernacular: 歡迎,各位師傅,歡迎各位。見你安好,我好高興。歡迎,好朋友。啊,我嘅老朋友!自從上次見你,你張臉掛上咗帷簾。你嚟丹麥係要挑戰我嘅鬍鬚?咩,我嘅年輕小姐同女主人!憑聖母,小姐你比上次見到時更接近天堂,差不多一個高底鞋嘅高度。求上帝,你嘅聲音,好似一塊流通不了嘅金幣,唔好喺環內破裂。各位師傅,歡迎你哋。我哋就好似法國放鷹人,見咩飛咩。我哋即刻要一段台詞。嚟,畀我哋嘗嘗你嘅本領。嚟,一段激情嘅台詞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 歡迎,各位師傅,歡迎各位。見你安好,我很高興。歡迎,好朋友。啊,我的老朋友!自從上次見你,你的臉掛上了帷簾。你來丹麥是要挑戰我的鬍鬚?什麼,我的年輕小姐和女主人!憑聖母,小姐你比上次見到時更接近天堂,差不多一個高底鞋的高度。求上帝,你的聲音,像一塊流通不了的金幣,不要在環內破裂。各位師傅,歡迎你們。我們就像法國放鷹人,見什麼飛什麼。我們立刻要一段台詞。來,讓我們嘗嘗你的本領。來,一段激情的台詞。

passages.title: First Player 第一伶人
passages.original: What speech, my lord?
passages.vernacular: 咩台詞,殿下?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 什麼台詞,殿下?

passages.title: Hamlet 哈姆雷特
passages.original: I heard thee speak me a speech once, but it was never acted, or if it was, not above once, for the play, I remember, pleased not the million, ’twas caviare to the general. But it was—as I received it, and others, whose judgements in such matters cried in the top of mine—an excellent play, well digested in the scenes, set down with as much modesty as cunning. I remember one said there were no sallets in the lines to make the matter savoury, nor no matter in the phrase that might indite the author of affectation, but called it an honest method, as wholesome as sweet, and by very much more handsome than fine. One speech in it, I chiefly loved. ’Twas Aeneas’ tale to Dido, and thereabout of it especially where he speaks of Priam’s slaughter. If it live in your memory, begin at this line, let me see, let me see: The rugged Pyrrhus, like th’ Hyrcanian beast,— It is not so: it begins with Pyrrhus— The rugged Pyrrhus, he whose sable arms, Black as his purpose, did the night resemble When he lay couched in the ominous horse, Hath now this dread and black complexion smear’d With heraldry more dismal. Head to foot Now is he total gules, horridly trick’d With blood of fathers, mothers, daughters, sons, Bak’d and impasted with the parching streets, That lend a tyrannous and a damned light To their vile murders. Roasted in wrath and fire, And thus o’ersized with coagulate gore, With eyes like carbuncles, the hellish Pyrrhus Old grandsire Priam seeks. So, proceed you.
passages.vernacular: 我曾聽你講過一段台詞,但從未上演,或者即使有,都唔超過一次,因為我記得,呢齣戲唔討好大眾,對一般人嚟講佢係魚子醬。不過佢係——正如我所領受,仲有其他判斷在呢種事上比我更高嘅人亦咁話——一齣優秀嘅戲,場面安排得好,寫得既謙遜又巧妙。我記得有人話,台詞入面冇沙律去令內容夠味,亦冇咩措辭可以控告作者矯揉造作,反而稱佢係誠實嘅手法,既健康又甜美,而且好睇多過精巧得多。其中有一段,我最愛。就係埃涅阿斯講畀狄多嘅故事,尤其係佢講到普里阿摩斯被殺嗰一段。如果你記得,從呢一行開始,等我諗諗,等我諗諗:「兇狠嘅皮洛斯,好似海爾卡尼亞猛獸——」唔係咁:佢係由皮洛斯開頭——「兇狠嘅皮洛斯,佢嘅黑色鎧甲,同佢嘅意圖一樣漆黑,當佢躲喺不祥嘅木馬中時,好似夜晚;而家佢呢副可怕漆黑嘅面貌,被更淒慘嘅紋章塗抹。由頭到腳,而家佢全身通紅,可怕地飾滿父親、母親、女兒、兒子嘅血,被燃燒嘅街道烘烤、糊成硬殼,嗰啲街道為佢哋污穢嘅謀殺借出殘暴而該死嘅光。被憤怒同烈火烤熱,又被凝結嘅血塊塗得更厚,雙眼似紅寶石,地獄般嘅皮洛斯去尋找老祖父普里阿摩斯。」好,你繼續。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我曾聽你說過一段台詞,但從未上演,或者即使有,也不超過一次,因為我記得,這齣戲不討好大眾,對一般人來說它是魚子醬。不過它是——正如我所領受,還有其他判斷在這種事上比我更高的人也這樣說——一齣優秀的戲,場面安排得好,寫得既謙遜又巧妙。我記得有人說,台詞裡沒有沙拉去使內容夠味,也沒什麼措辭可以控告作者矯揉造作,反而稱它是誠實的手法,既健康又甜美,而且好看多過精巧得多。其中有一段,我最愛。就是埃涅阿斯講給狄多的故事,尤其是他講到普里阿摩斯被殺那一段。如果你記得,從這一行開始,讓我想想,讓我想想:「兇狠的皮洛斯,像海爾卡尼亞猛獸——」不是這樣:它是由皮洛斯開頭——「兇狠的皮洛斯,他的黑色鎧甲,和他的意圖一樣漆黑,當他躲在不祥的木馬中時,像夜晚;現在他這副可怕漆黑的面貌,被更淒慘的紋章塗抹。由頭到腳,現在他全身通紅,可怕地飾滿父親、母親、女兒、兒子的血,被燃燒的街道烘烤、糊成硬殼,那些街道為他們污穢的謀殺借出殘暴而該死的光。被憤怒和烈火烤熱,又被凝結的血塊塗得更厚,雙眼像紅寶石,地獄般的皮洛斯去尋找老祖父普里阿摩斯。」好,你繼續。

passages.title: Polonius 波洛涅斯
passages.original: ’Fore God, my lord, well spoken, with good accent and good discretion.
passages.vernacular: 憑上帝,殿下,講得好,語調好,拿捏得宜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 憑上帝,殿下,說得好,語調好,拿捏得宜。

passages.title: First Player 第一伶人
passages.original: Anon he finds him, Striking too short at Greeks. His antique sword, Rebellious to his arm, lies where it falls, Repugnant to command. Unequal match’d, Pyrrhus at Priam drives, in rage strikes wide; But with the whiff and wind of his fell sword Th’unnerved father falls. Then senseless Ilium, Seeming to feel this blow, with flaming top Stoops to his base, and with a hideous crash Takes prisoner Pyrrhus’ ear. For lo, his sword, Which was declining on the milky head Of reverend Priam, seem’d i’ th’air to stick. So, as a painted tyrant, Pyrrhus stood, And like a neutral to his will and matter, Did nothing. But as we often see against some storm, A silence in the heavens, the rack stand still, The bold winds speechless, and the orb below As hush as death, anon the dreadful thunder Doth rend the region; so after Pyrrhus’ pause, Aroused vengeance sets him new a-work, And never did the Cyclops’ hammers fall On Mars’s armour, forg’d for proof eterne, With less remorse than Pyrrhus’ bleeding sword Now falls on Priam. Out, out, thou strumpet Fortune! All you gods, In general synod, take away her power; Break all the spokes and fellies from her wheel, And bowl the round nave down the hill of heaven, As low as to the fiends.
passages.vernacular: 「隨即佢搵到佢,向希臘人出擊但太短。佢古舊嘅劍,違抗佢嘅手臂,掉落喺邊就留喺邊,拒絕服從命令。實力懸殊,皮洛斯向普里阿摩斯猛衝,憤怒中揮擊落空;但單憑佢兇劍帶起嘅風聲同氣流,筋疲力竭嘅老父就倒下。然後無知覺嘅伊利翁,彷彿感受到呢一擊,頂端燃燒,向基座傾倒,以一聲可怕嘅崩塌,俘虜咗皮洛斯嘅耳朵。因為你睇,佢嘅劍,本來正落向可敬普里阿摩斯乳白嘅頭,彷彿喺半空中停住。於是,皮洛斯好似一個畫出嚟嘅暴君站著,對佢嘅意志同目標彷彿中立,乜都冇做。不過正如我哋常見風暴來臨前,天上一片寂靜,雲層停住,大膽嘅風啞口無言,下面嘅大地死寂,隨即可怕嘅雷聲撕裂天地;同樣,皮洛斯停頓之後,被喚醒嘅復仇心重新驅使佢行動,獨眼巨人嘅鎚落在馬爾斯為永恆而鍛造嘅盔甲上,都冇皮洛斯流血嘅劍而家落在普里阿摩斯身上咁無情。滾開,滾開,你呢個娼婦命運!所有神明,在全體會議中,奪走佢嘅權力;折斷佢車輪嘅所有輻條同輪圈,將圓形嘅輪轂從天堂之山滾落,一直滾到惡魔嗰裡!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「隨即他找到他,向希臘人出擊但太短。他古舊的劍,違抗他的手臂,掉落在哪就留在哪,拒絕服從命令。實力懸殊,皮洛斯向普里阿摩斯猛衝,憤怒中揮擊落空;但單憑他兇劍帶起的風聲和氣流,筋疲力竭的老父就倒下。然後無知覺的伊利翁,彷彿感受到這一擊,頂端燃燒,向基座傾倒,以一聲可怕的崩塌,俘虜了皮洛斯的耳朵。因為你看,他的劍,本來正落向可敬的普里阿摩斯乳白的頭,彷彿在半空中停住。於是,皮洛斯像一個畫出來的暴君站著,對他的意志和目標彷彿中立,什麼都沒做。不過正如我們常見風暴來臨前,天上一片寂靜,雲層停住,大膽的風啞口無言,下面的大地死寂,隨即可怕的雷聲撕裂天地;同樣,皮洛斯停頓之後,被喚醒的復仇心重新驅使他行動,獨眼巨人的鎚落在馬爾斯為永恆而鍛造的盔甲上,都沒有皮洛斯流血的劍現在落在普里阿摩斯身上那麼無情。滾開,滾開,你這個娼婦命運!所有神明,在全體會議中,奪走她的權力;折斷她車輪的所有輻條和輪圈,將圓形的輪轂從天堂之山滾落,一直滾到惡魔那裡!

passages.title: Polonius 波洛涅斯
passages.original: This is too long.
passages.vernacular: 太長。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 太長。

passages.title: Hamlet 哈姆雷特
passages.original: It shall to the barber’s, with your beard.—Prithee say on. He’s for a jig or a tale of bawdry, or he sleeps. Say on; come to Hecuba.
passages.vernacular: 佢同你嘅鬍子要一齊去理髮店。——請繼續講。佢喜歡跳舞或淫穢故事,否則就瞓。繼續;講到赫卡柏。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它和你的鬍子要一起去理髮店。——請繼續說。他喜歡跳舞或淫穢故事,否則就睡。繼續;說到赫卡柏。

passages.title: First Player 第一伶人
passages.original: But who, O who, had seen the mobled queen,—
passages.vernacular: 不過誰,啊誰,曾見過蒙面嘅王后——
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過誰,啊誰,曾見過蒙面的王后——

passages.title: Hamlet 哈姆雷特
passages.original: ‘The mobled queen’?
passages.vernacular: 「蒙面嘅王后」?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「蒙面的王后」?

passages.title: Polonius 波洛涅斯
passages.original: That’s good! ‘Mobled queen’ is good.
passages.vernacular: 好!「蒙面嘅王后」好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好!「蒙面的王后」好。

passages.title: First Player 第一伶人
passages.original: Run barefoot up and down, threat’ning the flames With bisson rheum. A clout upon that head Where late the diadem stood, and for a robe, About her lank and all o’erteemed loins, A blanket, in th’alarm of fear caught up— Who this had seen, with tongue in venom steep’d, ’Gainst Fortune’s state would treason have pronounc’d. But if the gods themselves did see her then, When she saw Pyrrhus make malicious sport In mincing with his sword her husband’s limbs, The instant burst of clamour that she made,— Unless things mortal move them not at all,— Would have made milch the burning eyes of heaven, And passion in the gods.
passages.vernacular: 「光腳跑來跑去,用盲目嘅淚水威脅火焰。頭上一塊破布,取代剛才戴王冠嘅地方,而腰間——生育過多、乾癟嘅腰——一張毯,喺驚恐嘅警報中隨手抓起——誰見到呢景,用浸過毒嘅舌頭,都會宣告反對命運之神嘅統治為叛逆。但如果眾神親眼見到佢嗰陣,當佢見皮洛斯用劍將丈夫四肢剁碎作惡意嘲弄,佢嗰一刻爆發嘅哀號——除非凡間事完全不能感動佢哋——會令天上燃燒嘅眼睛流淚,令眾神動情。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「光腳跑來跑去,用盲目的淚水威脅火焰。頭上一塊破布,取代剛才戴王冠的地方,而腰間——生育過多、乾癟的腰——一張毯,在驚恐的警報中隨手抓起——誰見到這景象,用浸過毒的舌頭,都會宣告反對命運之神的統治為叛逆。但如果眾神親眼見到她那時,當她見皮洛斯用劍將丈夫四肢剁碎作惡意嘲弄,她那一刻爆發的哀號——除非凡間事完全不能感動他們——會使天上燃燒的眼睛流淚,使眾神動情。」

passages.title: Polonius 波洛涅斯
passages.original: Look, where he has not turn’d his colour, and has tears in’s eyes. Pray you, no more.
passages.vernacular: 睇,佢面色冇變過,眼中有淚。請你,夠喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 看,他面色沒變過,眼中有淚。請你,夠了。

passages.title: Hamlet 哈姆雷特
passages.original: ’Tis well. I’ll have thee speak out the rest of this soon.—Good my lord, will you see the players well bestowed? Do you hear, let them be well used; for they are the abstracts and brief chronicles of the time. After your death you were better have a bad epitaph than their ill report while you live.
passages.vernacular: 好。我好快會叫你講完其餘部分。——好殿下,你可以安頓好呢班演員嗎?你聽到嗎,要好好款待佢哋;因為佢哋係時代嘅摘要同簡短編年史。你死後,與其有一段壞墓誌銘,不如生前免被佢哋講壞話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好。我很快會叫你說完其餘部分。——好大人,你可以安頓好這班演員嗎?你聽到嗎,要好好款待他們;因為他們是時代的摘要和簡短編年史。你死後,與其有一段壞墓誌銘,不如生前免被他們說壞話。

passages.title: Polonius 波洛涅斯
passages.original: My lord, I will use them according to their desert.
passages.vernacular: 殿下,我會按佢哋應得嘅對待佢哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 殿下,我會按他們應得的對待他們。

passages.title: Hamlet 哈姆雷特
passages.original: God’s bodikin, man, much better. Use every man after his desert, and who should ’scape whipping? Use them after your own honour and dignity. The less they deserve, the more merit is in your bounty. Take them in.
passages.vernacular: 天啊,老兄,要好得多。如果按每個人應得嘅對待佢,誰能逃過鞭打?按你自己嘅榮譽同尊嚴去對待佢哋。佢哋愈唔配得,你嘅慷慨就愈有價值。帶佢哋入去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 天啊,老兄,要好得多。如果按每個人應得的對待他,誰能逃過鞭打?按你自己的榮譽和尊嚴去對待他們。他們愈不配得,你的慷慨就愈有價值。帶他們進去。

passages.title: Polonius 波洛涅斯
passages.original: Come, sirs.
passages.vernacular: 嚟,各位。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來,各位。

passages.title: Hamlet 哈姆雷特
passages.original: Follow him, friends. We’ll hear a play tomorrow.
passages.vernacular: 跟住佢,朋友哋。我哋明日聽戲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 跟著他,朋友們。我們明天聽戲。

passages.original: [Exeunt Polonius with all the Players but the First.]
passages.vernacular: [波洛涅斯帶除第一個演員外嘅所有演員下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [波洛涅斯帶除第一個演員外的所有演員下。]

passages.title: Hamlet 哈姆雷特
passages.original: Dost thou hear me, old friend? Can you play The Murder of Gonzago?
passages.vernacular: 老朋友,你聽到我嗎?你可以演《岡扎古謀殺案》嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老朋友,你聽到我嗎?你可以演《岡扎古謀殺案》嗎?

passages.title: First Player 第一伶人
passages.original: Ay, my lord.
passages.vernacular: 可以,殿下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可以,殿下。

passages.title: Hamlet 哈姆雷特
passages.original: We’ll ha’t tomorrow night. You could for a need study a speech of some dozen or sixteen lines, which I would set down and insert in’t, could you not?
passages.vernacular: 我哋明晚演。必要時,你可以背熟一段十二或者十六行嘅台詞,我會寫低並加入佢,可以嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們明晚演。必要時,你可以背熟一段十二或者十六行的台詞,我會寫下並加入它,可以嗎?

passages.title: First Player 第一伶人
passages.original: Ay, my lord.
passages.vernacular: 可以,殿下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可以,殿下。

passages.title: Hamlet 哈姆雷特
passages.original: Very well. Follow that lord, and look you mock him not.
passages.vernacular: 好。跟住嗰位大人,留意唔好取笑佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好。跟著那位大人,留意不要取笑他。

passages.original: [Exit First Player.]
passages.vernacular: [第一個演員下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [第一個演員下。]

passages.original: [To Rosencrantz and Guildenstern] My good friends, I’ll leave you till night. You are welcome to Elsinore.
passages.vernacular: [對羅森克蘭茲同吉爾登斯特恩]我嘅好朋友,我離開你哋到夜晚。歡迎你哋嚟艾爾西諾。
passages.vernacularMandarin: [對羅森克蘭茲和吉爾登斯特恩]我的好朋友,我離開你們到夜晚。歡迎你們來艾爾西諾。

passages.title: Rosencrantz 羅森格蘭茲
passages.original: Good my lord.
passages.vernacular: 殿下慢走。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 殿下慢走。

passages.original: [Exeunt Rosencrantz and Guildenstern.]
passages.vernacular: [羅森克蘭茲同吉爾登斯特恩下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [羅森克蘭茲和吉爾登斯特恩下。]

passages.title: Hamlet 哈姆雷特
passages.original: Ay, so, God b’ wi’ ye. Now I am alone. O what a rogue and peasant slave am I! Is it not monstrous that this player here, But in a fiction, in a dream of passion, Could force his soul so to his own conceit That from her working all his visage wan’d; Tears in his eyes, distraction in’s aspect, A broken voice, and his whole function suiting With forms to his conceit? And all for nothing! For Hecuba? What’s Hecuba to him, or he to Hecuba, That he should weep for her? What would he do, Had he the motive and the cue for passion That I have? He would drown the stage with tears And cleave the general ear with horrid speech; Make mad the guilty, and appal the free, Confound the ignorant, and amaze indeed, The very faculties of eyes and ears. Yet I, A dull and muddy-mettled rascal, peak Like John-a-dreams, unpregnant of my cause, And can say nothing. No, not for a king Upon whose property and most dear life A damn’d defeat was made. Am I a coward? Who calls me villain, breaks my pate across? Plucks off my beard and blows it in my face? Tweaks me by the nose, gives me the lie i’ th’ throat As deep as to the lungs? Who does me this? Ha! ’Swounds, I should take it: for it cannot be But I am pigeon-liver’d, and lack gall To make oppression bitter, or ere this I should have fatted all the region kites With this slave’s offal. Bloody, bawdy villain! Remorseless, treacherous, lecherous, kindless villain! Oh vengeance! Why, what an ass am I! This is most brave, That I, the son of a dear father murder’d, Prompted to my revenge by heaven and hell, Must, like a whore, unpack my heart with words And fall a-cursing like a very drab, A scullion! Fie upon’t! Foh! About, my brain! I have heard That guilty creatures sitting at a play, Have by the very cunning of the scene, Been struck so to the soul that presently They have proclaim’d their malefactions. For murder, though it have no tongue, will speak With most miraculous organ. I’ll have these players Play something like the murder of my father Before mine uncle. I’ll observe his looks; I’ll tent him to the quick. If he but blench, I know my course. The spirit that I have seen May be the devil, and the devil hath power T’assume a pleasing shape, yea, and perhaps Out of my weakness and my melancholy, As he is very potent with such spirits, Abuses me to damn me. I’ll have grounds More relative than this. The play’s the thing Wherein I’ll catch the conscience of the King.
